sections.h:
Tuesday

D. pp. 137-138, par. 2

The Mother With The Child, And The Eternal Father.

In some experiences of infused contemplation Rosa sees the Mother with the Child beside the divine Father. A presence that leads one to consider the nature of the bond that associates them in the Economy of Salvation and that is an existential message for her:

«I saw my Eternal Father with smiling face, he pointed out a vacant place to me; and then Mary with the Child my Jesus in her arms in the act of offering him to me…» (M. 1.1, p. 39).

God's Economy toward her manifests a connection between her life and that of Mary with the Child.

In the light of the History of Salvation, the Mother with the Child and the presence of the Eternal Father attest the reality of Mary in God, who from eternity thought and created her with the most exalted dignity of being Mother of the Son begotten and not created.

For Rosa, then, in the perspective of the gift received, Mary is the Mother of Jesus, her Son and eternal Son of the Father; she is the Mother of God with her most exalted dignity in heaven and on earth, in her mission and function, in relation to creation and to the plan of the Incarnation and of Redemption.

Wednesday

TC pp. 154-157, «Numerous young women…I thought it to be the ordinance of my God»

Numerous young workwomen for a new field of the Lord.

At last, from afar voices were heard. Who can it be? A great quantity of girls, who with all their might ran to meet me! and I more than ever hastened my step. As soon as they saw me they exclaimed loudly:

- Blessed be you in the Lord! A terrible hurricane carried everything away from us and, however much we begged the Lord to come to our aid, seeing ourselves lost, we could obtain nothing. Only a young gentleman told us to travel this road, that we would find a farmer and that she would accept us to work in the vineyard of the Lord. And, from the marks he gave us, it is you!

And all vying with one another pressed close to me.

- Well then, tell me what was this gentleman like?

- Exceedingly handsome!

- And where did he stay?

- We do not know!

I gathered them and invited them to follow me, because there was still a road traced. And so they did. But after long walking, one began to say to me that she did not feel up to making so much of a journey, and so disastrous, and preferred to go back. There were no reasons to convince her. How much pain I suffered! But others still, in the end that half remained halfway. What my anxiety was I cannot describe.

At last we find a good shepherd and, greeting us, he invites us to his house. And what mercy! he makes us a gift of his estate, and begged me to have it worked for the greater glory of God. I did not delay in putting these workwomen all in their places and one of them I left as guide. A strong voice, which commanded me to do it as quickly as possible and to go back to help those who would not come with me.

Weary, without delay I turn back; but hardly had I gone a few steps when a rough man comes up to me and says to me:

- Run, for those creatures you left on the way are dying. I stop, seized by the thought that the voice I had heard so strongly was He, that I should go to their sufferings. They are the cause of their own harm and, surely, now they would want help. I was perplexed, when my angel comes up to me:

- Jesus forgave the lost little sheep and went seeking her to bring her back to the flock (cf. Lk 15:4-7). Charity must have neither reasons nor limits.

So, the voice was my angel's and, much mortified, I ran to find them again. Arrived at the first, they were badly hurt by the many ill-treatments received from the infernal dragon. At last arrived at the others, who lacked little of having fallen into the infernal precipice, gathered all together, we prostrated ourselves on the ground to thank the Most High and to beg his grace and mercy.

In this land of labor, where nothing but thorns and crosses is found, only the grace of God is the comfort of immortal souls, for whom there remains only the passage from this life to blessed eternity.

Continuing to reason, we came to a little farmhouse. My voice:

- Stop! for here there are good people and you will find where to put these poor peasant girls to work. It surprised me to see again those two good old people who had sheltered me another time, but far from these parts: they were other fields, the farmhouse different, but the two old people were those who welcomed me with great joy and handed over to me their estate, begging me to put my workwomen on it.

The estate set in order, I only lacked the one to leave to direct these inexperienced peasant girls. The good old woman, seeing me so thoughtful, begged me to tell her why I was worried, and I told her:

- Because I have no one to whom to entrust these workwomen. She offered herself and assured me that she would take great care of it, that I need not fear in continuing my journey, that, when I find her, I should send her to her. I thought it to be the ordinance of my God.

Thursday

Tr. pp. 38-40, «Material poverty…his dwelling will be glorious»

The material poverty to which the people of the covenant is subject is a prophecy and a reminder of the nothingness of the creature and of the all of God and of his grace (cf. Ps 25:9; 9:19). In this sense poverty contains the sum of all the virtues beginning with humility, with the lively sense of one's own nothingness, of one's own native insufficiencies worsened by original sin, and of one's own frailty before the mercy and the infinite generous richness of God's goodness, which puts no limits on his gifts, in order to restore to the human person the richness that had been granted in the act of creation. These gifts, wonderfully increased, are guaranteed and made admissible by the grace of the head of the mystical body: Jesus Christ.

It is then well understood how this long waiting for the Messiah was more acutely felt by the poor in material goods, tried by the poverty and misfortunes of slavery, exile, the loss of homeland, of people and of all well-being.

These experiences gave rise to the small and poor «remnant of Israel», which thus learned to live in fidelity to the demands of Revelation, awaiting the fulfilment of the Lord's promises. These were precisely the conditions willed by the God of the Covenant so that the goodness of the redeeming God might shine forth the better, even surpassing the goodness of God the creator.

Wishing now to sum up in two words the explicit and implicit, outward and inward prayer of the people of the Covenant marked by hope, enlivened by faith and by love grateful to God, we can without doubt identify it in the sigh of every soul that in the atmosphere of the covenant: «Come to save the people, come O redeeming God! Rend the shadow of waiting, come to free it from the slavery of guilt, come, O almighty and merciful God!».

St. Anne belongs to the people of the Covenant and particularly to the «small remnant», a truth deducible from God's own promise:

«Then those who feared the Lord spoke with one another… The Lord heeded and heard them… They shall be… my possession on the day when I act… For behold, the day comes, burning like an oven. Then all the arrogant and all evildoers will be stubble… but for you who fear my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings…» (Mal 3:16-20).

If she saw the sun of righteousness rise in her house, there is no doubt that St. Anne lived with such inner impetus the waiting made of hope, of faith, of full trust in the promises of the Most High, that she merited the grace of being chosen as mother of the Immaculate, dawn of Redemption, guarantee of the divine promises: «There shall come forth a shoot from the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots. And the Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and might, the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord.. In that day the root of Jesse shall stand as an ensign to the peoples… his dwelling shall be glorious» (Is 11:1-2.10ff.).

Friday

TC pp 218-220, «My voice: -keep walking like this…it is all the work of God»

My voice:

«Keep walking like this and you are doing well!»

Oh! but this darkness frightens me! Day never broke; but is it possible that it must be so long a night? I could bear it no more and began to weep loudly and to call my angel to come to my aid: nothing! And I kept on climbing without understanding how or where I was.

A most vivid light let me see that that darkness was not of the night, but because I was in an immense cavern and my path was in the middle of it; it was beautiful, but all varied: stretches all stony, others with thorn bushes and others with trees. How is it that down here, in so dark a cavern, there are plants with fruit? Oh! what pain if I should stray on so rugged a road! Oh! what fear! a strong trembling seized me. My strength begins to fail me and I feel myself fainting. A voice comes up to me and says to me:

«Gladly would I help you, but I do not know how. I too am in the dark and cannot understand you.»

«What pain!» I cried «Why do you not understand me? Who are you?»

«A shepherd who saw you at other times and you aroused my compassion; but this time I feel no compassion. This road of yours is your own journey: I find nothing to lean on to understand a road so high and mysterious.

«Have pity, I tell you, if you are a shepherd, and of God!»

Nothing! And I could not understand where he was.

«Are you alone in this cavern? He answered me:

«What cavern? I see and it is not dark at all!

At last he told me to address my prayer to a shepherd who could give a judgment about my darkness. My voice:

«Obey! but nothing is for you.»

Running I found him, at least I heard his voice. He told me that he had seen a shepherd and that he had told him that a creature was in this cavern and was groaning.

«Is it you?» he said to me.

«And how do you see me if I know no one?

«I know you well, and I must look at your path and then report to the one who sent me what there is in it of the great and mysterious, and whether it is of the Lord or you are off the way, and whether into this cavern supplied with delights, but for you dark without the least light, the Lord or the monster of darkness has brought you.

While he spoke, I listened, but without stopping. I said to him:

«Ah! of my path I am mistress and faithful slave of my Love. If he has brought me here into such sorrowful darkness, it can be nothing else but to purge my negligences in working his fields; and if I feel faint and wounded, I know I deserve it all. Clasped to the prayer of the Virgin, I run groping and weeping!

Having heard this, the good shepherd said to me in a faint voice:

«Do you want help?»

«No!

And I heard another voice: it was that of the first, who was also near that last. Here is what I heard:

«I assure you that here man has nothing to do: it is all the work of God.

Saturday

FS pp. 258-259, «She would like to make… November 1886»

She would like to make of each daughter of St. Anne a spokeswoman of Jesus to let all men hear the message of the Love that saves; that all might have the gift that she experiences when she feels herself a pure instrument of Him who makes her speak.

She wrote to her intimate Sr. A. Celsa Speranza:

«Jesus will put on your tongue words that not even you will know how you pronounced them… Love, and think that it was Jesus who spoke in your heart and you were his echo, another» (Letter undated, n. 76).

What matters is, first of all, to evangelize with life (Circular Letter 20-8-1895). One of the sisters testifies in the informative process: «She wanted and imposed on us to act as missionaries in the hospitals, first by our bearing and then by charity and, finally, by word» (Summ., p. 650).

Mother Rosa's apostolic heart had two moments of deep joy: one, when she gave her maternal embrace to the sixteen sisters of the first expedition that left for Latin America on 23 November 1878, an omen of rapid expansion on that continent; and the other, that day when she presented to Leo XIII the four members of the first mission to East Africa, November 1886.

21st Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 72-73, «Hope in the God of the Covenant… new creation»

Hope in the God of the Covenant who does not disappoint

Certainly this hope does not disappoint nor confound because it has as guarantor God himself made Man. On these divinely unshakable foundations «hope does not disappoint and cannot disappoint» (Rom 5:5).

Within the reduced people of Israel there is in fact a «small remnant», the family of St. Anne on whom God could count.

The great majority of the people, however, thought like the apostles themselves before the descent of the Holy Spirit. The most intimate friends of Jesus asked one another who among them would be the greatest in the new Kingdom now arrived and the mother of the two brothers goes so far as to ask Jesus for a privileged place for her sons. This was a purely human conception: we can see it in Jesus' answer to Peter who would dissuade him from facing passion and death «Get behind me, Satan! your language is the fruit of human wisdom. You are not thinking as God does, but as men do» (Mt 16:23). His is a very harsh answer, different from the ordinary language he used.

St. Anne then certainly merited to become the mother of Mary through hope in the coming of the Messiah and of his kingdom. This same hope Mary lived. Her sublime holiness gathered in herself all the hope of Israel and surpassed it to such a point that God could not further delay the fulfilment of His promises by choosing her as mother of the Messiah. With Her the promise of the Covenant goes beyond the borders of Israel and of its history. Upon her rest the good pleasure of the most holy Trinity to the point of meriting the most wonderful revelation of the reality of the awaited Messiah: «…he will be Son of God».

Mary most holy instills in our hearts too a new kind of hope: the certainty that the Holy Spirit is working a «new creation».

Monday

Tr. pp. 131-132, par. 3.3

Credible witnesses so that all people may open themselves to salvation

The daughters of St. Anne and all who belong to the Family of the Mother of the Immaculate are called to be a prophetic sign of the merciful love of the Father, of the unconditional offering of Christ Jesus, of hope, fruit of the Spirit.

By their very presence they seek to be credible witnesses for all people, so that they may open themselves to salvation and be able to share in the integral freedom introduced by Christ. For this reason they comfort, help, make their own the anxieties and concerns of those who suffer; they bring relief to the sick and to the marginalized, awakening their hope in the Lord Jesus and in his promises, and help them discover the precious essence of pain in the light of his passion.

In the suffering and the marginalized they moreover recognize and serve Christ Crucified who considers done to Himself what is done to the weakest, the most forgotten and the poorest, and they accompany with trust the hopes of humanity, orienting them toward the path of the covenant that will be definitively fulfilled in the beatific vision, in the splendor of the glory of the Father contemplated forever.

To accomplish this they second with vigilant readiness the action of the Spirit, and work diligently to gather around the Father the whole human family in the certainty that only God and his Kingdom are absolute.

Thus, with the whole Church, with prayer and with the heart, they call out day and night: come, Lord Jesus!

Tuesday

TC pp. 443-444, «The holy shepherd chosen by God… thank my God»

The holy shepherd chosen by God for His Work.

Many years ago it had been announced to me that I would have the fortune to meet a holy shepherd, that he would be the only one to put in good order the fields of my Master, and he would secure them so that no one in the future could give the workwomen any other direction, which for this poor slave would be a great relief, bringing back peace and a less laborious work with fear of succumbing under it.

As if awakened from a most sweet sleep, I found before me the shepherd announced to me. From his ways and from what my voice told me, it was he. The fear of erring kept me perplexed, my voice, with affirmative words, assured me it was he.

Several times thrown to the ground, clasped to the cross, I asked to be better assured. My voice:

- You will see the facts.

And then I felt an assurance placed within me. And my voice:

- It is he!

I no longer paid attention to my fear; but I informed him of everything, resolving to hide nothing from him. I submitted to him all the workwomen and perfectly found that he had the true spirit of my Master: upright, for inexorable justice, charity equal for all (yet I never told him what passed within me, no, only small things), jealous of the fields, vigilant over order, most delicate to the point of scruple. Oh! I was not mistaken. While I prayed fervently, my Lord let me see how dear he was to him and that he had chosen him for his Work, and that he would do very well, that every action of his would be done to the advantage of the fields. God took much delight in it.

How calm I feel in this! As if leaning on a great poplar, I rest in everything; in the struggles against certain shepherds I do not fear. Calmly I have my dreams. Oh! how I can thank my God!

Wednesday

TC pp. 361-362, «Refreshed and guided by St. Michael…today you will find the field»

Refreshed and guided by Saint Michael the Archangel.

Without caring at all for myself, I went in search to find what my voice had told me. Night falls and nothing is yet seen. What, was I deceived? I was weak and felt a fierce need to take food; neither farms nor churches were to be seen. Alone! From exhaustion I began to weep:

- My angel Saint Michael, ah! come to my aid! Leaning against a great tree, weeping I stood. In this position I fell asleep. A gentle voice wakes me. Who was it? A heavenly messenger who, in a basket, brought me bread.

- Oh! dear angel! tell me, who sent you?

- God.

- But I - I said with a deep sigh - how gladly would I long to feed on Him alone!

And I did not dare take the bread. He, with peace, urges me to eat. I took the bread, kissed it and then, kneeling, set myself to eat it. Oh my Love! from you comes this treasure! And then, turning to the messenger, I said to him:

When he sent me this bread, did he bless it? Tell me: what did he tell you to tell me? nothing?

He answered:

- That you eat!

- But - I answered - I am not at all satisfied: I want Him! And I began to weep, and he comforted me.

When I had finished eating, he gave me water to drink: it was a most exquisite liquor. I did not notice that it was night: nothing! The moon was shining most brightly. He began to say: - We must set out.

- Well then, will you do me the charity of accompanying me?

He answered:

- Surely, so it is my charge.

I gave a deep sigh: Oh my God! you I want, you I want!

He answered:

- Let us hasten our step, for in a few hours you will find him.

So it was. As soon as dawn came, the sound of bells was heard. But on this journey he with sweet reasonings taught me, giving me so much knowledge: how the soul in union with God is blessed, is nourished… Oh! how those hours passed for me! I felt nothing of weariness. Oh! would that day had never come!

As soon as the church was seen, he vanished. I entered the temple of my God and in Him I found myself wholly. I asked him whether the voice that sent me on this journey was his ordinance. He answered me:

- Yes! and today you will find the field.

Thursday

FS p. 155, «Her personal existence … that every pain is a delight to me»

Her personal existence was almost a pilgrimage in the dark through the desert, gladdened only by some refreshing oasis. Only one who follows Jesus to Golgotha and to the agony of the cross shares in the triumph of his glory.

«On Tabor one can stay only to take a little refreshment, and Jesus is accustomed to take there the weak souls who, if he does not refresh them, die on the way; but the strong (go) ever forward, spurred on, until they have arrived at Golgotha and there crucified with Him, to rise all beautiful, luminous, and enter triumphant into glory in heaven» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 12-8-1870).

Precisely this hope of eternal glory must sustain loving souls in the sufferings of this life; here is the time to suffer, there will be the time to enjoy.

«A brief suffering for an eternal enjoying», she often repeats. And she likes to quote the well-known couplet of Saint Francis of Assisi: So great is the good I await - that every pain is a delight to me (cf. Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 3-10-1867; to Sr. A. Aquilina Gilardoni: 5-1-1886).

Friday

D. p. 73, «The Beloved anticipates her… Oh, my Love!»

The Beloved anticipates her and enlightens her on the paths of the Father. He grants her graces, but at the cost of her personal sacrifice. He makes her a sharer in the redeeming Economy by letting her understand that the healing of a person, the conversion of a sinner or the peace of a city are the fruit of a personal offering joined to the unique and unrepeatable one of Christ Jesus:

«The goodness and charity of my Beloved made up for all my miseries. He told me that he would heal her (a Superior) but that the washing - of that wound she had - with my blood was needed, and so I did, shedding much of it through a harsh discipline of blood. Again the chastisement made me see Rome and then I said to my Good: ah! for charity have pity on that people, and for the prayers of the good souls in that city, may you be appeased and forgive, suspending the chastisement.

He made me see the duplicity of hearts and… Oh, my Love! The Pope! the Pope! dear Pius IX, oh, how he made me see how much I loved him. He will have nothing… a thousand other things he made me see, but all beautiful ones that lifted me from the sad dejection in which I found myself. Oh, if I could tell what I saw and felt on the day of Corpus Domini. Oh, my Love! (M. 1.1, p. 53).

Saturday

TC pp. 332-335, «A poor woman approaches me… and so I received great instructions»

A poor woman approaches me, and says to me:

- What are you looking for at this hour?

- I am looking for a charitable soul who would lodge me even in the stable with the animals.

- Where do you come from?

- I came from very distant roads to find charity to bring to some poor brides of the Lord, who live on the bread of alms.

- Who are you? - she added

- Oh! - I answered with a long sigh - a poor slave of the Lord!

She looked at me and then said to me:

- Come with me: I have only one room and one bed.

- Oh! may you be blessed a thousand times! Your charity will be rewarded.

We made our way to her poor dwelling. Oh! how many prayers I said along the way for this poor creature! Having arrived home, wonder! there was a table sumptuously laid, with exquisite dishes. Seeing them, she cries out, as much from joy as from surprise:

- Who, who has prepared this? Oh! how happy I am to have you!

- What are you saying, good woman? It is I who find myself led by one beside whom I do not deserve to be. Take me where you put the rubbish, that is enough for me.

This poor woman begins to weep:

- Either you come with me to eat or you make me die of sorrow!

My voice:

- Satisfy her!

And so I did. I took only a little bread, because weariness kept me from eating. And I thanked her. She wanted to leave me her room.

- Oh! that will never be! God, good woman, will reward you just the same as if this wretched one had accepted.

And I placed myself at the entrance of her room, where there was a small dark corridor; and there I stayed praying all night: I prayed for my benefactress and for those who had made me suffer so much that day; and I thanked God for the great grace of sending me so good a creature who gave me shelter.

While doing this, I fell into ecstasy; I felt I know not what in my soul, which rested sweetly. Oh! what a soft bed! it was something delightful. So I spent the night without noticing.

Returned to the world of miseries, full of strength and vigor, I would have fought against an army: so full did I feel of the strength of my God! I heard that the woman was awake too; I thanked her and went to the temple to receive my God at once. So it was. My voice, while I made my thanksgiving:

- Make again the round you made yesterday and beg alms for love of me.

So I did. What wonder! those whom the day before I had found so fierce, who would have beaten me, welcomed me with such kindness, and I gathered great provisions. After walking two hours, I had gathered enough; and the voice of nature, which always feared to meet with blows, suggested that I go away; but my voice, which held sovereign dominion over all my faculties (was contrary):

- No! - I answered - My voice told me to make again the whole round I made yesterday.

And so, running, I made the whole round again, and what I gathered was extraordinary, and I no longer knew where to put it. I finished at night. Some wanted to give me food, some lodging; I thanked them all very much, but accepted nothing.

On the way, there was one last door left for me to ask at. It was already dark, and I was so afraid! But these too gave me alms. I wondered what I would do: behold, at the end of the street the good woman who was waiting for me. I thanked her, accepted the lodging as on the other night, resting just as well, except that she had me find in that corner a straw mattress and a pillow. I accepted a little bread; and then I suffered from having found that bed, because I feared I would no longer have the rest of the past night. Having finished that meal, having come near that bed, my intention was not to lie down on it, but my voice (said to me):

- Lie down, for it is I who had it prepared. Patience! I said to myself, and I lay down. My voice:

- Why so unwillingly?

- My God, no!

I lay down, and asked excuse and pardon of my God, after he had had so much charity as to inspire that woman to prepare this for me. Sweet Love of mine! Oh! you know why: I would have wished to spend this night like the other past one. Having said this, I remained absorbed in my God and so I received great instructions.

22nd Sunday in Ordinary Time

TC pp. 363-366, «Diversity of God's love… and made the work beautiful»

The diversity of God's love compared with that of creatures.

I would never have left this temple; but it was his will that I leave it. So, without further remark, I set out. After walking two hours and more, behold what the voice had told me. Oh magnificence! it was something delightful. I entered fields of varied and diverse flowers; many graceful young girls vied to offer them to me. I accepted many; but I always had in mind the word: «You will find flowers and laurel to weave». What shall I do? - I kept saying to myself. And they kept bringing me more. There was laurel. One of them, older and bolder, said to me:

- See all these fields, how beautiful they are and so full of flowers!

- Yes - I answered.

- Well, since we do not know how to weave them, once picked they wither and become foul.

- Oh! - I added - Why do you not try to give them to Jesus?

- Tell us how we should do it.

- Let us make a garland and give it to that church which has a field attached, but a poor one; the farmhouse where the poor workers are is so ill-kept that those poor little ones live badly there.

These creatures listened to me.

- Well then! - they said to me - weave as many as you like, take them to those creatures, as well as to the church you speak of.

I did not delay in setting to work. And they helped me with great pleasure. How happy I felt, because I was doing great things with those bouquets. I took a quantity of laurel.

- This - I said - is for you, who with such generosity help the poor and the brides of the Lord, as well as his church. You will be crowned with laurel for eternity. And I shall strive to weave it so well, putting into it all the ability my Master gives me.

One of them, who more than the others remained silent, comes up to me and says:

- Could I too not learn together with you the same lessons your Master gives you?

- Oh! yes, certainly! He - I began to say - is all for all, and greatly rejoices when a creature shows herself eager to learn. Yes, come with me and you will see how you will learn to weave roses and lilies… I was forgetting the laurel: above all else my Jesus gives importance to this, and how graceful is his garland!

Without thinking, carried away by joy, I exclaimed: My Love! My Love! Enchanted, she said to me:

- But earlier you told us that you are alone and a slave of the Lord.

- And what you say is true - I answered her - Is he not my God, my Love?

- What? - she retorted, almost as if I had blasphemed - Do you speak of love?

- Yes, my God is all love toward his creatures.

I realized that she was altogether a stranger to this subject and begged her to listen to me. Meanwhile all the others around drew near and I instructed them on all the points of our holy Religion, going on to make known to them the diversity of God's love compared with that of creatures; that the heart of the creature has need of love and how, not knowing the sublimity of God's love, they love creatures. In God's love is all the divine essence and it has neither limits nor end; that of creatures is deceitful and soon vanishes, withers like the rose plucked from the plant and put in the sun: the disillusion of the perishable things of earth is plainly seen; but the love of my God, Master and Lord, burns ever more in the heart of the creature and finally, with its rays, carries it off and consumes it in his divine most sweet ether. Oh yes, Love!

I cannot describe the effects these words of mine had on the hearts of these poor creatures. The one who more than all was touched by grace said to me:

- With you I will go! Let us gather my whole share of this field and take it with us.

The others gave me a great deal, begging me to return as soon as possible. Having taken leave together with that dear creature, we brought those treasures to the farmhouse and to the church. Oh Love! She learned so well to love and became beloved of my Good! She was a rose just opened into a graceful white lily, which under the shade of purity had been kept for the most pure heart of Jesus. She soon tasted the delicacies of the Spouse, and by her deeds could better teach what she herself experienced. She did great works with all those varied treasures and she guarded the Lord's fields for me very well. The workers multiplied to everyone's amazement. Who was working? My Master! in appearance there was the creature, but in fact it was the Creator who gave the direction and made the work beautiful.

Monday

Tr. pp. 58-59, par. 3.4

A prophetic, priestly and royal people sent to proclaim the Kingdom

Christ, the great prophet, who by the witness of his life and the power of his word proclaimed the kingdom of the Father, fulfills his prophetic office until the full manifestation of his glory (LG 35).

In him all the faithful, made sharers in his mystical body through the outpouring of his Holy Spirit, form a holy and royal priesthood, offer to God spiritual sacrifices through him and proclaim the wonders of him who called them out of darkness and welcomed them into his marvelous light. There is therefore no member in the Church who does not have a part in the mission of the whole body, but each of them must sanctify Jesus in his heart and bear witness to him with a spirit of prophecy (cf. PO 2) so that the power of the Gospel may shine forth. The Church is in fact a prophetic, priestly people, not only thanks to baptism, but also to the Eucharist where Jesus exercises his eternal priesthood which is at once sacrifice and sacrament. The sacrifice of the Mass is the same sacrifice of the cross.

In the Eucharist Jesus, eternal priest, continues to immolate himself mystically, exercising his priesthood as head of the Church, his mystical body. Baptism, which makes the Christian holy because it confers sanctifying grace, lays the foundations of Christian perfection, and makes the baptized a sharer in the priesthood of Jesus and in his prophetic power. The members of Mother Rosa's charismatic Family, committing themselves to live their baptism intensely, grow in the prophetic dimension, which reveals the saving and merciful love of God, and cooperate with all their strength in the expansion and growth of the Kingdom of Christ in the world, serving Christ in others and leading to him, with humility and patience, all their brothers and sisters (cf. LG 35;36).

Tuesday

Tr. pp. 143-144, «Mother Rosa firmly believed… we wait for it with perseverance»

Mother Rosa firmly believed in God's plan, and so she did not spare her life, always hoping, even against all hope, in him, her Good, her strength and her defender: «Who will accuse the elect of God? It is God who justifies. Who will condemn? Christ Jesus who died, or rather, who was raised, is at the right hand of God and intercedes for us. Who will separate us, then, from the love of Christ? Will tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or the sword?

As it is written: for your sake we are being put to death all day long, we are regarded as sheep to be slaughtered.

No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us».

This same certainty must grow in us so that we may experience in life, in total surrender to the Father, how «neither death, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord» (Rom 8:38-39).

To be children in the Son is our destiny, but it is still the object of our hope. «In hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope; for who hopes for what one already sees? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with perseverance» (Rom 8:24-25).

Wednesday

Tr. pp. 94-96, «Jesus is our temple…just as Mother Rosa did»

Jesus is our temple. From the moment of the incarnation he became the temple in which we must raise our prayer to the Father. The Church is our teacher, concluding every prayer «through our Lord Jesus Christ, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, one God, for ever and ever». What a temple! In this temple we are invited to remain continually. God, however, was not content to give us so most holy a temple. He wished to adorn it with the most fantastic vestibule that the hand of the supreme divine artist could design, or engrave in the soul and Immaculate heart of Mary and build, until creating that divine work which is precisely the mother of the Redeemer and of all humanity: «Wisdom has built her house, she has hewn her seven pillars» (Prov 9:1).

With the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit he carved in Mary's soul the most splendid vestibule possible to the intelligent and powerful art of God, creator and restorer of fallen nature. When one wishes to enter the temple that is Jesus Christ, the entrance is sure. But if most holy Mary is the vestibule that leads immediately to the temple that is Jesus Christ, St. Anne, the mother of the Immaculate, is the solemn preceding architecture, worked likewise by the Holy Spirit, which leads in a manner worthy of God to the vestibule and to the temple. It is a logical consequence.

When one truly loves the Lord, when one thinks that he is more intimate to us than we are to ourselves, one ends by making of one's whole life a dialogue of intimacy; of filial abandonment to the Father, in full adherence to the divine will, with total offering of oneself in every daily circumstance, in uninterrupted union with Jesus in the Eucharist; of docility to the Holy Spirit; of total surrender to the most holy Trinity; of tenderness toward most holy Mary, our sweetest mother; and of love and filial trust in St. Anne, the angels and the saints, just as Mother Rosa did.

Thursday

Tr. pp. 139-140, par. 1.2

Christ Jesus, the Holy One by essence, is he who makes «all the saints»

The Church reflects anew on the apostle's admonition, who, urging the faithful to charity, exhorts them to have in themselves the same sentiments that were in Christ Jesus, who emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, becoming obedient even unto death (cf. Phil 2:7-8), and for our sake, though rich, became poor (cf. 2 Cor 8:9).

Although the disciples must always manifest the imitation and witness of this charity and humility of Christ, Mother Church rejoices to find in her bosom many men and women who follow more closely this self-emptying of the Savior and show it more clearly by embracing poverty and renouncing their own will; for the love of God, in what concerns perfection, they submit themselves to man beyond the strict measure of the precept, in order to conform themselves more fully to the obedient Christ. All the faithful, therefore, are invited and obliged to seek the holiness and perfection of their own state. For this reason let all strive to direct their affections rightly, so that from the use of the things of this world and from attachment to riches, contrary to the spirit of evangelical poverty, they may not be hindered from tending toward perfect charity, as the apostle indeed warns: «Let those who deal with this world not become engrossed in it, for the form of this world is passing away» (cf. LG 42).

These texts, chosen from among the many inspired ones, constitute a brief complete summary of spiritual doctrine, and more exactly the best commentary on the program «Turned toward the fullness of communion with the God of the Covenant, fulfillment of every hope».

Friday

Tr. pp. 152-153, «Christ the Lord…all holiness: Father, Son and Holy Spirit»

«Christ the Lord, High Priest taken from among men (cf. Heb 5:1-5), made the new people «a kingdom of priests for God, his Father» (Rev 1:6; cf. 5:9-10). By regeneration and the anointing of the Holy Spirit the baptized are consecrated to be a spiritual house and a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices through all the works of the Christian, and to proclaim the marvels of him who called them out of darkness into his marvelous light (cf. 1 Pet 2:4-10). Therefore all the disciples of Christ, persevering in prayer and praising God together (cf. Acts 2:42-47), should present themselves as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God (cf. Rom 12:1), bear witness to Christ everywhere and, to those who ask, give an account of the hope of eternal life that is in them (cf. 1 Pet 3:15)» (LG 10). All men, as they have the vocation to Christianity, so they have actually and virtually the vocation to the Catholic Church.

«The people of God shares also in Christ's prophetic office by spreading everywhere a living witness to him, above all by a life of faith and charity and by offering to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess his name (Heb 13:15)» (LG 12). The Church, made up of the baptized and of believers, for her part is always holy (as we profess in the Creed) and sanctifying. Sin too, in fact, does not destroy in the sinner the sanctifying effect of baptism: a seed, a root of a possible return to God and of the consequent sanctification.

The holiness of the Church has its icon in most holy Mary Immaculate. And as the Immaculate is the Mother of the Word made man, so the Church, continually, through the sacraments begets and regenerates holiness, thanks to her indissoluble union with Christ, her most holy spouse, the holy one by essence, the first principle of all holiness: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

Saturday

TC pp. 474-475, «You still have too much to work, my beloved…No! out! - he said shouting»

«You still have too much to work, my beloved!»

Overcome by weariness, I began to complain and said: But how long this road is! I am tired, I am cold and hungry, nothing is to be found here, my eye cannot see even a haystack or a tree: all dry rocks! Surely night will come and, if this road goes on like this, I shall die of sorrow. So for me there is no more hope of getting out of here; everything before me is frightening.

And I walked. The road grew ever worse and everything that lay before me. The sun sets, hunger makes itself strongly felt, my strength already fails: a great panic seizes me of having to succumb in the midst of that great stony ground. I look here and there to see if I can find a blade of grass, because I would gladly have eaten it, but nothing! My throat dry, my palate dry and not even a brook in sight to take a sip of water. I feel myself fainting and kneel with hands joined. I called my Master, my Lord, and, crying out, told him that I was dying:

- Ah! come, help me: I am lost!

And I fainted. A gentle voice says to me:

- Rise!

- Oh my Love! I am dying, you know?

He, with a smile:

- No! too much, my beloved, you have to work! Do not fear: my strength needs nothing. Run: before night you will find help. And he leaves me. Must I go away from here? Oh no! Here is my Good. And I kept my gaze fixed on that place where I had seen and heard him. But my voice:

- Hasten to obey!

I seemed a giant of strength; I do not know whether I flew or truly walked. At nightfall, I see in the distance a bell tower and hear its pealing. Oh my Love! it is your dwelling: a temple! tomorrow I shall feed on you. Oh! what a strong embrace I shall give you in this your heart! A thousand sweet and loving words I repeated and in all haste I flew.

Arrived at the door of the temple, the sacristan was closing the doors. I begged and implored him to let me in: it was no use. He said a thousand vile things to me: that I was a vagabond, a wicked woman…, and a thousand other outlandish words. I answered nothing, and curled up on a step. This grumbler, seeing me so, grew even angrier and wanted to kick me so that I would go away.

- Ah! for pity's sake, let me stay here until tomorrow comes.

- No! out! - he said shouting.

23rd Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 131-132, par. 3.3

Credible witnesses so that all people may open themselves to salvation

The daughters of St. Anne and all who belong to the Family of the Mother of the Immaculate are called to be a prophetic sign of the merciful love of the Father, of the unconditional offering of Christ Jesus, of hope, fruit of the Spirit.

By their very presence they seek to be credible witnesses to all people, so that they may open themselves to salvation and be able to share in the integral freedom introduced by Christ. For this reason they comfort, help, make their own the anxieties and concerns of those who suffer; they bring relief to the sick and the marginalized, awakening their hope in the Lord Jesus and in his promises, and help them discover the precious essence of suffering in the light of his passion.

In the suffering and the marginalized they moreover recognize and serve Christ Crucified, who considers done to himself what is done to the weakest, the most forgotten and the poorest, and they accompany with confidence the hopes of man, orienting them toward the way of the covenant that will be definitively fulfilled in the beatific vision, in the splendor of the glory of the Father contemplated eternally.

To accomplish this they follow with watchful readiness the action of the Spirit, and work eagerly to gather around the Father the whole human family, in the certainty that God alone and his Kingdom are absolute.

Thus, with the whole Church, with prayer and with the heart, they cry out day and night: come, Lord Jesus!

Monday

Tr. pp. 130-131, par. 3.2

In the Church, with a specific mission

Choosing Mary Immaculate as their model, they become a sign of hope for the man of today in the preferential action for the poorest, knowing how to identify and relieve the new forms of poverty. They therefore commit themselves to integral liberation in the sense of that freedom with which Christ has set us free (as St. Paul warns). Christ has set us free so that we might remain free: «Stand firm, therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery» (Gal 5:1).

This is the great freedom that sprang from the redeeming death of Christ. An immensely profound freedom that rescues man from the slavery of Satan and of sin, not in the sense restricted to the mere «political» freedom to which the freedom of Christ is sometimes reduced, but in the sense of integral freedom, a prophetic sign of hope for the man of today.

Tuesday

Tr. p. 120, «Wholly devoted… Be silent and listen»

«Wholly devoted to the salvation of the world, a divine work that transcends all human strength and all human wisdom, the Sisters [and Brothers] strive to discover day by day, in the intimacy of personal and communal dialogue with God, his saving will and to open themselves to the action of the Spirit so as to become docile instruments of the Father's mercy».

«Aware of this priceless spiritual patrimony of Mother Rosa, her daughters and those who follow her and live her message will cultivate prayer, applying themselves each day to meditation on Sacred Scripture [according to the Constitutions and the statutes of each form of life in which the same charism is lived].

The interiorization of the Word is not possible without the inner silence that allows us to listen to God, who manifests himself as «a sound of sheer silence», speaks to the heart and asks his creatures: «Be silent and listen».

Wednesday

TC pp. 176-177, «My thirsting soul seeks him… without any merit»

My thirsting soul seeks him everywhere and burns with strong desire to speak to him and to unite itself to him as to its only center.

- In his will your soul finds him again.

- Oh! it is too sweet to do it and in everything to find a contrary, for one who does not yet possess it, to one's own will! I feel a strong shudder at the mere thought that man clings so much to this will of his, so contrary to that of God. How to make him understand and still more taste this sweetness of God's will? Man seems a slave, because he does not know how to renounce what chains him in order to have another who guides him in everything and with great sweetness leads him to the blessed life. He answered me:

- Man is blind to his own will and suffers for it without any merit.»

Thursday

FS pp. 181-182, «The account…that good which she could»

The account she herself gave of what happened in Piacenza on March 31, 1869 because of the slanderous accusations raised by the superior of the house herself, is the best testimony of her behavior in similar cases and, above all, of her ready and generous forgiveness (M 1.2, pp. 21-28).

After summarizing the five persecutions suffered in the years 1868 and 1869, «fireworks from every side», she adds: «Only one thing comforts me, and that is that no rancor ever remained in me toward those who caused me so much pain, whoever they were, rather I feel a very great affection for them and for them I increased my prayers, and I always sought to do them the good I could» (M 1.2, pp. 28-31).

Friday

FS p. 293, «The goal toward which… run with exactness»

The goal toward which such formation tended was the holiness of each of the daughters of St. Anne.

«May the Lord make you saints and great saints», she repeats in her letters. She wrote to Sr. A. Celsa Speranza: «Tell me, do you believe that I want only one thing: your sanctification? Yes, it is true. Well, I, great wretch that I am, do not cease asking my God that, through the merits of my dear Crucified, he sanctify you all. In clasping myself to him when I am in my poor room, oh! with what strength I clasp you in his Heart! O sweet Love! Yes, my dear daughter, seek me in him and I promise you that you will always find me» (Letter undated, n. 76).

In the Memoirs we find supplications such as this: «I would wish them all to be according to your Heart, my Love!» (M 11.2, p. 82f). And in a circular of 1893: «We cherish a great desire to be able to see you all according to the heart of God»

(Circ. Letter: 23-4-1893). And, as a sure means of walking according to God's will and attaining holiness in the life embraced, she insists on the observance of the Rules, «the pivot that holds the wheel steady and makes it run with exactness» (Circ. Letter: 20-2-1893).

Saturday

FS p. 213, «Each day she made… upon them the choicest blessings»

Each day she made as it were an oblation to the eternal Father, in the mercy seat of the Heart of Jesus, of her Institute, not as an organized and operating structure, but as a living reality, made up of individual persons, each with her vocation, with her effort of sanctification, with her responsibilities, with her problems. It was her prayer as a foundress:

«My God! to you I entrust these creatures whom you have entrusted to me. Now I place them for all this time in the Heart of your Son Jesus, and may you cover them with heavenly dew, that they may be defended from the slightest encounter. In this loving retreat of the Heart of Jesus may they learn the true school of your divine Love. My God, bless them and strengthen them in suffering, pour upon them the choicest blessings» (Letter to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti: 25-5-1871).

24th Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 48-49, «God who makes himself a creature…because bound to him «

God who makes himself a creature, taking the form of a «servant»; to draw near to us God becomes like one of us, with a gesture of infinite love and, in the end, lets himself be seized, condemned to death, scourged, crowned with thorns, crucified and even stripped of everything, dying naked on the cross.

How could the charism of Mother Rosa Gattorno, who so loved the Crucified, be explained otherwise, without this theological, ascetical-mystical background that so strikingly characterizes her life?

The poverty of Jesus is also full, absolute, total acceptance of and adherence to the Father's will, so as to be not only the Mediator (behold the new personal Covenant between God and man), but the Redeemer who takes upon himself the guilt of all men and, with his sorrowful passion, death and resurrection, obtains full victory over sin, over hell and over death. In this way he restores to man in superabundant measure the divine life of grace, becoming, with luminous teachings, and even more with his examples, light of the world for all humanity (Jn 8:12).

Jesus Christ, the Word incarnate, is in fact the new Covenant in the strong sense: God and man are in him one single Person, the Mediator by essence between God and man, at once priest and victim together, repairer of all the faults and failures of humanity. He is the first, inexhaustible source, the firmest rock of hope for all humanity, the liberator from the prince of this world (the devil), the guarantor of salvation and of eternal life, and the principle of a hope immensely deeper than that of the Old Testament, a hope that will never fail because bound to him.

Monday

FS pp. 217-218, «The treasure of the Eucharistic presence…to produce it in others»

The treasure of the Eucharistic presence.

The «great mystery of our faith» had become the continual object of her adoration and her love. She remained absorbed before this «sole and immense treasure of our soul» (Letter to Emilia di Fitalia: 4-9-1889). Very often this faith was transformed into experience through vision, especially when in adoration with the Blessed Sacrament exposed; but also when she contemplated him enclosed in the tabernacle. She prayed thus one day in 1866: «Satisfy me, for pity's sake, with your love! Oh! why do I not remain forever before your monstrance where, my Beloved, you are enclosed? What are five, six hours a day? Nothing! Let me remain beside you without moving any more… Light of my eyes, sweet Love of mine! If men knew you, surely they would leave everything and come to the foot of your altar to enjoy your delights. But how can I make them understand?…» (M 1.1, p. 43f).

She was happy when, on her visit to Pius IX, in January 1866, she obtained from the Pontiff an autograph granting her the faculty of keeping the Blessed Sacrament at home (FIOCCHI, I, p. 109). In Piacenza she wished to have her little cell adjoining the chapel; thus, even during the night, she directed to Jesus in the sacrament her acts of adoration and her affections through the little window opened in the wall.

She frequently speaks of the long stretches of time she spent absorbed in close union with him, sometimes even the whole night (M 3, p. 79; 4.1, pp. 12f, 18; 4.4, pp. 26f, 95f, 114f).

One of the forms of her piety, always original, was to travel in spirit to the chapels of the various houses of the Institute to unite herself with her spiritual daughters in the homage of love to the Lord present in the tabernacle (M 4.1, p. 87f).

She taught them to turn to him in difficult moments: «If you find yourself downcast, run to the church and cry out, weep with Jesus, and then, your tears dried, back to work, all to all and full of sweet unction to produce it in others» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 13-5-1872).

Tuesday

FS pp. 273-274, «Spiritual guide… and turned wholly to Jesus»

Spiritual guide and solicitous mother.

We already know the foundress's maternal affection for the spiritual daughters God gave her. Feeling responsible before him who called them and entrusted them to her care gives her love a sense of presence among them, joined to a lively pastoral awareness that makes her all solicitude for their good. Her letters to the superiors and to individual sisters attest her delicate maternal attentions, almost meticulous, both as regards bodily health and the interests of the spirit. To express how close she feels to each one she uses terms full of spontaneous cordiality: «I have you with me… everywhere I go»

- «I feel all the sorrows you have and I told the Lord to transfer them onto my shoulders, for my breast already shares the pain»

- «I have you at my right hand and every morning I commend you to God, my only All»

- «You are nearer to me than if I had you at my side…»

- «I always pray and can say in all truth that no morning passes when I leave the church without praying in particular for all of you».

She not only shares the afflictions and vicissitudes of the good religious, who console her heart, but also the situations and struggles of those who are in danger of infidelity to the commitments undertaken; she prays for them, offers her penances for them. She writes on September 19, 1892: «I had promised the discipline of blood if my Good would grant me the conversion of a daughter of St. Anne who was in great danger of losing her vocation… I saw her free and turned wholly to Jesus» (M 12.2, p. 5f).

Wednesday

FS pp. 282-283, «Mother Rosa was…in the burning heart of Jesus»

Mother Rosa was convinced that the good running of the Institute depends, first of all, on the wise choice of superiors and on their responsible care for the good of the sisters. Certainly, the rapid growth of the Work with the multiplication of houses in Italy, in America and in Africa made it difficult to find suitable superiors for every community. From her correspondence with them and, above all, from the circulars, often very harsh, one deduces that not all were equal to the task entrusted to them. The foundress feels it her duty to denounce with raw sincerity the unevangelical behavior of the superiors, but also to form them and guide them in the right way of governing. Besides the correspondence kept up with each one, she makes use of the aforementioned circulars and, in a special way, of the conferences on the occasion of visits, gathering them by zones, and of the general chapters, which are usually preceded by a course of spiritual exercises.

She has an ideal image of the superior, whose traits she seeks to instill on every occasion. First of all, she bitterly stigmatizes the ambition to become a superior, «accursed vice that reigns in the Institute», as well as «pride, vanity, vainglory» which dominates in many, as she was able to verify in her visits; she prays the Lord to give her back «daughters full of his love, humble, ready to accept any office, from superior to laundress, from superior to cook» (Circ. Letter 15-6-1894).

The first task of a superior is to be guide and support of her sisters in fidelity to their vocation, knowing that «they will have to render account to God for their souls» (Circ. Letter 1890, 20-1-1892). But she cannot be an effective guide if she herself is not a model and example for them: «Superiors are the shadow of the other religious, for all run after them and go as the shadow shows them the way» (Letter to Sr. Francesca Camisa: 13-5-1872)

- «The superior must be the lighthouse that guides all to the safe harbor… Care for the interests of your heavenly Spouse, win souls for him. Courage, then, and holy emulation with your beloved sisters in the advancement of the virtues!» (Letter to Sr. A. Gerarda Canovi: 30-4-1900)

- «Superiors are the candelabra which, as their torch burns, the others entrusted to them are lit in turn and, true burning torches of sacrifice and love, seek to consume themselves in the burning Heart of Jesus (Circ. Letter: 3-3-1897).

Thursday

TC pp. 421-423, «The seed you will sow… the task the Master requires»

«See to it that the seed you sow is good».

Meanwhile it seemed that they had gone away, but I always felt movement now here, now there. My God! I began to say: what am I to do? Must I still find myself in the midst of such wretched people? My voice:

- Come out, for good people await you; for several days they have been looking for you, because they need workers.

I kiss the ground and rise to go out. The door was closed, but the sacristan was not long in arriving. He opened it for me and I thanked him, and he, so good, asked me to promise to commend him to the most holy Virgin. I promised to do so, being much obliged to him.

After a few steps, behold two good men who stop me and ask me for workers for a large field, which they wanted to entrust entirely to my companions. They take me to see the field, and it was very vast, but uncultivated. I was so surprised to see most graceful valleys and immense fields, all for us. I thought to myself: but the dark night in which I find myself? My voice:

- This is the fruit of your great sufferings. See to it that the seed you sow is good: so beautiful and graceful will the harvest be.

Those good people accompanied me to my old cottage, leaving me with (the request) to return soon to those graceful fields.

The thought of the good seed gave me great anxiety and, placed at the feet of my dear

Crucifix, I asked him to tell me what seed I had to send there, for I did not trust my own choice. Oh! how soon I had the answer: This (seed) shall be the workers and you shall not leave them until you have seen that the fields are well in order.

I did not delay in carrying out what I understood. But hard and painful was the toil. The fields were uncultivated. My God! what to do? The more I labored, the less I could ever see the field clean. At last I threw myself on the ground and, weeping, asked the eternal Father to tell me what was there that bore such bad fruit: what was it? A shepherd who was not after the heart of God! I did not delay in making strong prayers that he be removed. My God! The workers, instead of being all fervent and intent on giving glory to their Lord by working well in his vineyard, uprooting the weeds, what were they doing? with their bad cultivation it happened that this evil weed was doubled.

Oh what mercy of my God! He sent me three good workers; two, in fact, truly full of love and zeal for the Lord's work, who found the means to remove him.

Oh! how many blessings from the heights of heaven must he have poured in great abundance upon their heads. Oh! how my Lord protects them for me, sustaining them in all their steps, so that not even they notice it; but I many times see clearly what my God works in them! And woe if they knew it! But I, who hold them dear and near, guard them as beloved workers of my Good. Oh my sweet Master! who in such small hearts pour out your treasures, without those who possess them knowing it! Now then he has placed this worthy and holy shepherd, who makes the workers run so well, and they give that task which the Master requires.

Friday

FS pp. 252-253, «Not only did she encourage… and have the good fortune to belong to it»

Not only did she encourage the sisters to spend themselves in initiatives responding to social realities, but she also stirred up the benefactors and friends of the Institute. In her letters to the Princess of Fitalia she insistently urges the charity of this spiritual daughter of hers to be generous toward «the wretched both in soul and in body». On August 18, 1892 she wrote to her asking her to help a poor mother with four children, abandoned by her husband. On November 15, 1896 she expressed her concern for so many poor in the coming winter, which was announced as harsh. Again on September 13, 1897: «If you do not help me, what will become of my poor this winter?».

She knew, however, how to distinguish mere beneficence from authentic Christian charity, which gives with love and with humility, without protectionism or bureaucratic structures. She wrote in the circular of January 20, 1892: «Be humble with the poor; always remember that you are the last and the most wretched of all the creatures who render their service to the Church and have the good fortune to belong to it».

Saturday

TC pp. 457-458, «So tired I fell asleep…your Master awaits you».

So tired I fell asleep leaning against a tree trunk, which served me as a pillow. I slept deeply. A voice from afar woke me, calling me by name, that I might go to the aid of people who were sure of their deed, that is, that after the beating I had received I could no longer move. But, once awake, I found myself full of vigor. My voice:

- Run to the people who want to plot against my fields; and do not stop until you have an order from me.

Full of vigor I rose and, running, reached the field. Set to work, the field took vigor and so all heard that I was approaching them. They were frightened and tried to come to themselves. The workers eagerly worked the soil. God let me see, through one of the workers, how beautiful the great field of his Work had become. My voice:

- It is not time to stop, but rather it is necessary to run this narrow path to arrive where your Master awaits you.

25th Sunday in Ordinary Time

FS pp. 143-144, «A mother's heart… on seeing a soul relieved»

A mother's heart toward the daughters given by the Lord.

In the evangelical pedagogy of St. Francis and St. Clare of Assisi the welcoming of every brother and sister is emphasized as a gift of the Lord who called them. Mother Rosa has the same gratitude toward God the Father who cares for her Work, sending her such numerous ranks of daughters of St. Anne; she has a mother's heart for each one individually. She follows them with her thought and affection to the houses where they are assigned, rejoices at the good news of their successes, of their progress in holiness, as on the contrary she grieves and suffers real torment when one is unfaithful to her vocation, when another falls ill, when God calls them to himself through death. As we have seen, she possesses the gift - charismatic or telepathic as it may be - of tuning in to the situations of her distant daughters as well as that of sensing their dispositions when they are present.

Her day is divided between the time given to prayer and that devoted to correspondence with the sisters, especially with the superiors, from whom she wants to be informed about the needs of each subject. In the thousands of letters, written both alone and with the help of secretaries, one seems to feel the beat of a near and tender heart, whether when she consoles and encourages or when she reproves and admonishes. We also know how she welcomed and helped individual sisters on her frequent visits to the houses.

In the midst of the adversities she had to experience as a foundress, she found comfort in this maternal solicitude. She wrote in 1878:

«Recovered from sorrow, nothing is desired, nothing seems able to be sweet on earth, nothing! Only one thing (the soul) feels it can taste: it is charity. Oh! what joy it feels in being able to do good and to see to putting right, setting at peace with God, one who has strayed! Yes, in charity the soul rejoices in everything, takes part in it and, in seeing the well-being of creatures, feels great pleasure. Sacrifice, whatever pain it cost, always turns out a consolation on seeing a soul relieved» (M 1.2, p. 110).

Monday

FS pp. 245-246, «Zeal for the good…the choicest of his blessings»

Zeal for the good of her spiritual daughters.

Freed by God's will from family ties, yet without extinguishing the flame of love for her own, Mother Rosa lived intensely for her new religious family, loving with a mother's heart each of the daughters of St. Anne, a love translated into solicitous concern, care, sharing of personal situations, longing for their spiritual progress and their fidelity to the commitments undertaken in profession.

First of all she wanted to see in the communities fraternal union, enlivened by a generous, understanding and welcoming charity, to the point of «giving one's life» in service to others (cf. Letter to Sr. Francesca Camisa: 23-4-1867).

In her letters to the superiors she expresses her joy when she hears that such a climate of union exists: «You cannot believe how much consolation I felt on hearing how well you are in agreement among yourselves. O blessed Charity! Good daughter! May God pour upon your head the choicest of his blessings!» (Letter to Sr. A. Battistina Bertuzzi: 28-8-1880).

Tuesday

FS pp. 256-257, «Rosa's heart… to make everyone feel what I feel!»

The heart of Rosa Gattorno was a volcano in constant activity, insatiable for love. Here is an outpouring of hers in a letter to Sr. A. Celsa Speranza:

«I would like to draw the whole world, give to all, feed all. Oh! from my veins if only I could make gold flow for the poor! Do you know what I would do? Myself, vein by vein, I would want to draw it out until they were left dry. Oh! would I be satisfied? No! it is too ardent!…» (Letter undated, n. 76).

One could compose a fine anthology from the effusions of her longing to make known and loved her dear Good, which leap out from the pages of her spiritual diary. Here are some: «My Good, how can I make you known to all the world? Oh! how many there are who do not know you! and those who have known you flee from you for never having seen you. I would like to run everywhere and cry out loud that all should come to love you» (Year 1862: M 1.1, p. 30).

«Oh! why do not all love you? See, O my Good, the burning thirst I have to save souls?» (M 1.1, p. 33).

«O my Love! make use for once of this miserable instrument of yours to revive the faith and the conversion of sinners!»

- «All souls, come! Ah! love Jesus, do not offend him!… I would have run through every street crying out that they should love Jesus. I threw myself face down on the ground and strongly asked the eternal Father to let me die a martyr to save the souls redeemed by him. Am I not your instrument? (Year 1867: M 1.1, pp. 60, 119).

«O my Love! how I feel myself burn with desire to make you known and loved by all! May your name be blessed by all tongues. My God! Oh! if only I could make everyone feel what I feel!» (M 1.2, p. 87).

Wednesday

FS pp. 254-255, «She taught…I do not direct it to him»

She taught the same spirituality to the daughters of St. Anne, that is, how to ground charity in seeing Christ in the needy and the suffering. In the same year she wrote to the sisters of the hospital of Cento: «Take comfort, you who labor for your Jesus. Ah! you always converse with Jesus, because in touching those sick with charity, you touch Jesus… In those infirm creatures Jesus is found. Ah! what a thought, my daughters! I assure you I feel myself dying with desire to come to be with you, to share in your works of charity…»

- «Seeing Jesus in the sick, how easy the meditation on the Passion of Jesus will be for you!» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 23-4-1867; 7-1867).

It is, however, interesting to note an evolution with the passing of the years, almost a purification of the motives of apostolic charity, the effect of a higher identification with the supreme Good. On January 18, 1875 Mother Rosa made the following profound introspection: «Creatures, little by little, become for me an object to cultivate and love, no longer as I still know I felt a sensible compassion for their ills, or wished them all holy, yes, but regarding them as if in the help and good I did them, or at least thought I did them, I found in them some pleasure, which the charity done to them seemed to me bound to bring them.

Now I find nothing, nothing: purely my Good. Not even the smallest of created things do I know how to regard with a simple glance, unless I first direct this too to him…» (M 4.3, p. 18f).

Thursday

FS p. 293, «She wrote to Sr. A. Celsa Speranza makes run with exactness»

She wrote to Sr. A. Celsa Speranza: «Tell me, do you believe that I want only one thing: your sanctification? Yes, it is true. Well, I, great wretch that I am, do not cease asking my God that, through the merits of my dear Crucified, he sanctify you all. In clasping myself to him when I am in my poor room, oh! with what strength I clasp you in his Heart! O sweet Love! Yes, my dear daughter, seek me in him and I promise you that you will always find me» (Letter undated, n. 76).

In the Memoirs we find supplications such as this: «I would wish them all to be according to your Heart, my Love!» (M 11.2, p. 82f). And in a circular of 1893: «We cherish a great desire to be able to see you all according to the heart of God»

(Circ. Letter: 23-4-1893). And, as a sure means of walking according to God's will and attaining holiness in the life embraced, she insists on the observance of the Rules, «the pivot that holds the wheel steady and makes it run with exactness» (Circ. Letter: 20-2-1893).

Friday

FS pp. 212-213, «Her mother's heart… choicest blessings «

Her mother's heart, when she writes to the daughters of St. Anne, finds no more fitting way to express her affection to them than to meet each one in the Heart of Jesus. It would be endless to try to gather the warm expressions in which she affirms at once her love for the Lord and for the addressee.

Each day she made as it were an oblation to the eternal Father, in the mercy seat of the Heart of Jesus, of her Institute, not as an organized and operating structure, but as a living reality, made up of individual persons, each with her vocation, with her effort of sanctification, with her responsibilities, with her problems. It was her prayer as a foundress:

«My God! to you I entrust these creatures whom you have entrusted to me. Now I place them for all this time in the Heart of your Son Jesus, and may you cover them with heavenly dew, that they may be defended from the slightest encounter. In this loving retreat of the Heart of Jesus may they learn the true school of your divine Love. My God, bless them and strengthen them in suffering, pour upon them the choicest blessings» (Letter to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti: 25-5-1871).

Saturday

TC pp. 337-338, «Rise, quietly… Majesty of a God»

- Rise, and quietly go and see what is happening. The wrongdoers have entered and are trying to get into my temple.

I noticed at once and found that it was true; but on sensing that there were people there, they fled and could do nothing to that temple nor to the brides of the Lord.

How tired I was! how I felt myself failing! I stayed at the feet of my God, waiting for the hour when I could possess him; and meanwhile I told him that I felt very ill and that he should hurry to come, because I felt my strength failing. Inwardly I had a great longing to rest. Having my Love with me, forgetful of everything and of myself too, I told him all that I had done. I would offer you my sufferings, but I am ashamed, because in comparison with yours, who suffered for me, I feel myself full of shame. Oh my angel Saint Michael! adorn a little what I suffer and what I suffered and did, and then you, if you think fit, bring it to the feet of the Lord. Oh! how happy I would be if he laid it upon his most holy feet! But I do not find myself worthy enough to be offered to the Majesty of a God.

26th Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp 140-142, par. 1.3

The Trinity, source and origin of all holiness

Holiness is the goal of creation and of redemption. «Be holy, for I am holy» (Lev 11:44; 11:45; 19:2; 20:7; 20:26; 21:8) God had already said to the chosen people of the old Covenant, and it can be said that all of God's interventions, directly or indirectly through the Prophets, are a call to holiness.

The universal vocation to holiness is therefore not a novelty of recent centuries. It is a divine imperative imprinted in human nature itself from creation, which has holiness as its purpose, just as redemption does.

In both the three divine persons are engaged: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. To the Father is particularly attributed the concept of principle, principle of every principle and of all reality and therefore also of creation; to the Son redemption; to the Holy Spirit sanctification.

Such a distinction of functions is theologically logical. If holiness consists in the perfection of charity, as the Second Vatican Council puts it, the Holy Spirit is charity itself, the third Person of the most holy Trinity.

The Father created us; the Son redeemed us and made us children of God; the Holy Spirit sanctifies us with an action always at work. His presence, silent and discreet, is recognized by the dynamism of love it arouses (cf. The Gift of God…, pp. 101ff.).

The experience of Mother Rosa attests the manifold workings of the Holy Spirit and urges us to adhere with love to each divine person so as to become docile, as she was, to their initiative: «Those who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God» (cf. Rom 8:14); «Do you not know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit dwells in you?» (cf. 1 Cor 3:16).

Let us make our own, contemplating them, all the attributes that he let Mother Rosa experience: sanctifying grace, creative activity, fire of love, light that enlightens minds and conscience, physician of souls, spiritual guide, tireless worker, voice that guides and directs in the work of the Father and in that of Jesus, interior strength, sweet consoler.

Let us also repeat frequently the prayers to the Holy Spirit, as the Church, teacher of prayer, invokes him in the Liturgy of the Holy Spirit: «Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love».

And with his coming we shall experience that his action is the active, working presence of God's mercy in the soul, bound to the merits of Jesus the redeemer in accordance with what the new Testament reveals to us.

Monday

FS pp. 40-42, «Rosa Gattorno possessed…great cordiality»

Rosa Gattorno possessed to an eminent degree the treasure that, humanly speaking, best characterizes the normal woman: the capacity to attune herself to what is good, beautiful and pleasant in life and to avoid what is morally deformed or unworthy; the gift of intuiting people's inner situations and of feeling close to those who suffer; the sense of the particular… When such a treasure is translated into the gift of oneself, we have the ideal image of the wife and mother of a family, who lives wholly for her own, or that of the consecrated woman who immolates herself for God and for others under the impulse of love.

Mother Rosa was a woman of delicately sensitive heart. Here too it is her letters that offer us the most eloquent testimony. She always keeps in mind the person of the addressee, with her particular traits, beginning with the name, which she knows how to insert very opportunely in order to reach the heart, with the state of her health, with her problems.

She worries, like the most solicitous mother, whether the sisters and the girls entrusted to them have enough food, whether they are sheltered from the cold… Some of her recommendations to the superiors may serve as examples:

«How it grieves me to hear that you are cold! My Jesus, give them your fire, so they will be sheltered. Dear Francesca, I think all the blankets were quilted; if you lack any, tell the steward… Tell the steward also to provide you with winter clothes, with little jackets, as we agreed, and with blankets. For charity's sake, cover yourselves!»

- «Console poor little Carlotta, take care of her and have compassion… I recommend the little girls to you and that you see that they are well covered at night, so they do not catch a cough; and the little ones, their heads clean…» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 10-10-1867, 2-7-1869; to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 25-9-1870).

Sensitive to the needs and situations of others, she was equally grateful for the attentions she received both from the sisters and from other people. Her letters are full of sentiments of gratitude, in terms of great cordiality.

Tuesday

Tr. pp. 113-114, «In Christ Jesus we all share… perfect communion with him»

In Christ Jesus we all share in his uniqueness and in the infinite benevolence of God the Father toward his Only-begotten.

In Jesus we are loved by the Father as the Father loves the Son who loved us unto death on the cross.

What a marvel the reality of the new Covenant contains, and to what richness of perfection Jesus has brought it! The grandeur, the security, the indissolubility of the new lets us appreciate the old better. The marvelous bond of the redeeming Covenant becomes a grand motive and foundation of hope.

In this perspective Christian life and holiness rest on such firm pivots that they cannot fail to become witness for those who accept them and live them in fullness, to the point of proclaiming them by life, example, word and action made charity toward God, our brothers and sisters.

It is not possible to identify with Jesus through prayer, the sacraments, above all the Eucharist, without becoming one with him. And since Jesus is one with the Father and the Holy Spirit, the spiritual Family of Mother Rosa realizes the thought and example of Jesus by letting itself be guided by the Spirit on the itinerary that leads it to full adherence to the Father's will and to perfect communion with him.

Wednesday

Tr. pp. 135-137, Preamble

Stretching Forward to the Fullness of Communion with the God of the Covenant, Fulfillment of Every Hope

The goal that the Lord points out to us as fullness of life in him implies movement, tension toward communion with him, the object of our hope, and constant discernment in order to set aside whatever can hinder the attainment of the end.

This indispensable condition of the «race» toward God we find in the inspired texts, in the doctrine of the Church and in the example of the saints, not least in Mother Rosa.

The radicalness of her spiritual impetus to advance rapidly toward the goal finds full confirmation in the pedagogy indicated by God throughout the Bible, but appears even more evident in some texts:
