«whatever gains I had, these I have come to regard as loss because of Christ. More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord. For his sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and I regard them as rubbish, in order that I may gain Christ and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but one that comes through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God based on faith. I want to know him and the power of his resurrection and the sharing of his sufferings by becoming like him in his death, if somehow I may attain the resurrection from the dead. Not that I have already obtained this or have already reached the goal; but I press on to make it my own, because Christ Jesus has made me his own. Brothers and sisters, I do not consider that I have made it my own; but this one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus» (cf. Phil 3:7-14).

Here, precisely, is a sacred text inspired by God, which clearly defines the vocation to holiness in general, and which illumines in particular the spiritual itinerary that Mother Rosa left as an inheritance to the Institute she founded

This is the spirituality of the Covenant:

- of the old Covenant, resting on the historical experience of God, on the Law;

- of the new Covenant, rooted primarily in faith in Jesus Christ.

Faith in him, in his divinity, fills the soul with hope and with supernatural optimism.

Thursday

TC p. 297, «With your blind obedience… everything spoke to me of love «

- With your blind obedience, with the love of carrying out God's orders, you have gained much, and the strength you desire the Lord grants you entirely.

It was a second! And I, strong as a giant, cleared the fields. And I set out on my path, running full of ardor for the glory of God and to seek his will in everything.

I reasoned about the matter and deeply felt keen sorrow. My voice:

- Enough! you must forget: love, for beloved you are!

Oh! sweet Love! how can I come to be able to do something pleasing to your being? Having said this, rapt, I do not know whether I walked with my feet on the ground or rather, as I believe, flew. In an Eden of Paradise I roused myself: everything spoke to me of love!

Friday

D. pp. 83-85, par. 3

The Voice again with the usual gentleness: try, it is my wish, and then I said, no, this Voice is my Good because I know it too well and the ugly one who speaks to me in a muffled way is the dragon. And at once I set to, indeed I made these irons myself and then I put them on. They were most atrocious points on a hide and I felt nothing, not even that night, they were most gentle pains. Oh! sweet Love what did I receive as a gift? Oh! sweetness (rapt in him I enjoyed the most beautiful and dear delights, illuminations) he taught me so many beautiful things» (M. 1.1, p. 138).

Adherence to God, through love, opens the soul to receive a new light. In the new horizon she sees clearly the holiness of God and everything in her and in others that is disharmonious.

From this light a new tension is born, which causes a suffering all the greater as it makes the soul perceive the intensity of her natural attachments.

Here is how Rosa describes this interior dynamism, the light that illumines her and the testimony of mercy of her Good: «To suffer and to rejoice. Oh! how useful these lights are to me, in a flash I see everything. Oh! what I feel, how I feel myself all aflame and I set about correcting that fault with such force because it is an offense to my Good. Be silent, heartless ones, why do you offend my dear Crucified? What has he done to you that you (offend him) so barbarously? I feel so much sorrow, but Jesus is silent. By the depths of his immense mercy, he suffers and does not punish. Oh! my Love, so many times I beg him to take from me this pain I suffer» (M. 1.1, p. 140).

The things that Jesus heard from his Father (cf. Jn 15:15), and makes known to her in mystical union, must not be forgotten.

They are his words and his divine interventions that weave her personal history and that of the Work. These interventions and words, her Good insists several times, she must set down on paper. Since he is the light of her path, she obeys even though she cannot foresee that this light will illumine the path of all those who will follow her in the ways of God.

From her testimony on this we receive confirmation:

«All for my Good, and so I stayed many days and months without writing, but of this he made me a just reproach, yet so gentle and sweet that I did not know what to answer, only: forgive me my Good. - Tell me why you do not write? - Oh! my Love, how can I? - At night half an hour for a note and then in time you will resume. - Oh! sweetness without equal, yes, my Good, I will not delay in doing it» (M. 1.1, p. 155). Thanks to these written sources, born of obedience to Jesus, we are able to reconstruct the authentic history of Rosa with her Good and Lord. It is a profession of faith in him present in history, through which he continues to manifest himself to those who develop the capacity to perceive and contemplate his Presence.

Saturday

FS p. 23, «And she knew how to instill courage… at rest for an eternity «

And she knew how to instill courage in her collaborators, in the superiors, in individual sisters and in other persons who confided in her. There is hardly a letter of hers in which the word does not leap out: Courage! Here are some of the words of encouragement we find in her letters to the sisters, amid vibrant expressions of affection:

«My dear child, come, courage!» - «Be of good heart, for heaven is favorable to you!» - «Courage, my dear! let us work, for then we shall rest in bliss. Stand firm, do not fear!» - «Patience, my dear, courage!… courage!» - «My beloved ones, courage, for one day you will see your God and you will enjoy your labors» - «Courage, and all confidence in the good God!» - «Courage, for in the moment of trial one needs courage and patience, peace and resignation. With this everything is obtained and every obstacle is overcome» - «Courage! If the road is closed on every side, we must go forward by dint of sweat of blood, until we have a drop left in our veins!» - «First commend yourself to God, and then forward with courage!» - «Courage, my daughter! for one day we shall taste the fruit of the blood and sweat shed in our labors!» - «Courage, forward! for one day we shall be at rest for an eternity!».

27th Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 128-130, par. 3.1

The daughters of St. Anne, and the other members of the Family, in the expectation of the Lord who comes, build the kingdom in poverty of heart and maternal and paternal self-giving, working in the Church according to a specific mission; they collaborate in the saving work of Christ bearing in their hearts a single passion: the Kingdom of God and the glory of the Father, following the example of the foundress.

They therefore strive for the growth of the holy faith, the conversion of sinners and service to their brothers and sisters, made sign and instrument of the Father's merciful love for all people. Inserted in the reality of the local church they are its leaven of communion, witnesses of hope and presence of proclamation, and they build the kingdom in poverty of heart and maternal and paternal self-giving.

As St. Anne awaited the fulfillment of the promises, the one sent by the Father, so they too, while they hope in the glorious manifestation of the Lord, burning with zeal like Mother Rosa, commit themselves to making him known to the whole world in the certainty that God has worked, works and will continue to work great things in people thanks to prayer and to our industrious apostolic activity, even when the cross of Jesus, physical or spiritual, invites us to walk, at least in part, the way of Calvary.

And the cross and the Crucified whom Mother Rosa loved with such ardor and generous devotion, just as the Psalm says: «Lord, my rock and my fortress, my deliverer, my God, my rock in whom I take refuge, my shield and stronghold, my mighty salvation. The waves of death surrounded me, raging torrents overwhelmed me; already deadly snares were closing on me. In my distress I called upon the Lord, in my anguish I cried to my God, from his temple he heard my voice, my cry reached his ears» (Psalm 18:3.7).

In these words of the Psalm the great sufferings, mystical too, of the foundress Mother are well foreshadowed, she who knew how to unite hope and love, joy and sorrow, «rejoicing like a strong man to run his course» (Psalm 19:6).

She knew how to walk the way of holiness and of the apostolate, in the footsteps of the suffering and crucified Christ, almost repeating with Jesus: «I have a baptism with which to be baptized - the baptism of blood - and how I am constrained until it is accomplished» (Lk 12:50). And those words spoken on the eve of the passion: «I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer» (Lk 22:15).

Monday

TC pp. 149-150, «Along the way I found…an eternity of joys»

Along the way I found my angel Saint Michael, who accompanied me to the farmhouse. At first sight of me, these good people kissed my habit and showered me with kindnesses; they wanted to give me something to refresh myself, but I did not need their refreshment, only that of my God. All gathered around, I began to speak of my God, that only he and for him must we live. A graceful peasant woman rose and, coming near, told me that she was warning me about speaking so much of God, because certain people were in that house who would do me harm. And she told me of that gentleman who had led many people, with his feigned manners, to perdition. How can it be? - I thought to myself - and yet my angel brought me here, and surely it was he.

When she had finished her account, behold that very gentleman wished to speak to me and, withdrawing to a corner, told me that he knew I was in great need for the cultivation of a field and that he had brought me large coins, so that I could continue to take on workers to make the field flourish ever more. With what pain I took that money! I looked at him and trembled, ever firm in my place. I said to him:

- This charity of yours may my God return to you a hundredfold. But more than this I would feel happy if it were granted me to hear you counted among those who love God so much. He remained pensive, and then said to me:

- What advantage shall I have in loving that God who is so much on your mind?

- Oh! - I exclaimed with force - the advantage of eternal life, filled with every good and, forever, an eternity of joys!

Tuesday

Tr. pp. 117-118, par. 1.2

Co-responsibility in fraternal life

The Church is essentially a mystery of communion, «a people brought into unity from the unity of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit» (cf. LG 4).

Fraternal life mirrors the depth and richness of such a mystery, taking shape as a human space inhabited by the Trinity, which thus extends into history the gifts of communion proper to the three divine persons.

All this requires a path of personal and communal growth, learning to overcome conflicts, growing in the capacity for forgiveness, in the exercise of discernment in the light of the Holy Spirit, knowing how to create unity in diversity, fostering and taking part in dialogue, on the unattainable model of most holy Mary.

All the members of the charismatic Family of Mother Rosa are called to bear lovingly one another's burdens, loving the cross as she did, remaining serene in trials and joyful in hope, never forgetting that a charism lived in fullness translates the Gospel, in particular the Gospel of the beatitudes, proclaimed by Jesus in his programmatic discourse, in which he lets it be understood that every virtue and every suffering and contradiction borne for love of God brings into the soul a beginning of Paradise, in the continual memory of the suffering Jesus and of Mary Immaculate-Sorrowful, mother of Grace and Mercy, mother of Hope.

To live, however, a style of life that is a witness of fraternity and a proclamation of hope demands a deep life of prayer and of gratuitous self-giving.

Wednesday

Tr. pp. 95-96, «When one truly loves the Lord…with the divine Master»

When one truly loves the Lord, when one thinks that he is more intimate to us than we are to ourselves, one ends by making of one's whole life a dialogue of intimacy; of filial abandonment to the Father, in full adherence to the divine will, with total offering of oneself in every daily circumstance, in uninterrupted union with Jesus in the Eucharist; of docility to the Holy Spirit; of total surrender to the most holy Trinity; of tenderness toward most holy Mary, our sweetest mother; and of love and filial trust in St. Anne, the angels and the saints, just as Mother Rosa did.

An unsurpassable model of prayer remains for us the one taught by Jesus himself: «Our Father who art in heaven», which contains the truth of our sonship and daughterhood before God creator, redeemer, sanctifier, and for that very reason opens us also to the experience of universal brotherhood with all the members of the human community who, thanks to the mystery of the incarnation, become a single family in Christ in the communion and sharing of the material and spiritual goods generously bestowed on all by the infinite goodness of God.

All the members of the human family either are Christians or have the vocation to know and love Jesus Christ. With him, in him and through him we can call our God «Father».

Hence the urgency of missionary and evangelizing activity so that the «virtual» call may become actual and explicit through knowledge of the Gospel.

While he was teaching the «Our Father» Jesus was surrounded by his disciples. Still today he continues to be present among those who pray with faith. The scene of Jesus praying to the Father with his disciples has therefore become the paradigm of Christian prayer. When the Christian, consecrated persons, the whole Church, and in her all the members of the Family of the holy Mother, take up an attitude of prayer, Jesus prays with them, and they pray with the divine Master.

Thursday

Tr. p. 101, «The experience of being… Come, Lord Jesus»

The experience of being brothers and sisters in Christ Jesus

When we keep in mind our belonging to the Church and are well persuaded that we form one body and one Church with all Christians, then prayer becomes universally choral. If then we are well convinced that the pilgrim Church and the heavenly Church are also one single thing, then our prayer is surely echoed by the angels and the saints of Paradise. A valid foundation is constituted by the spiritual patrimony of the Family of the mother of the Immaculate. «Following the example of Mother Rosa, the Daughters of St. Anne [and all the members of her spiritual Family] «having in view solely and above all else God», strive to join contemplation with apostolic service, and docile to the Holy Spirit seek in the intimacy of prayer the encounter with the Father so as to realize with him, in imitation of Christ, a relationship of tender and intense filial love. Faithful therefore to Jesus' exhortation to pray without ceasing and taking inspiration from the poor and humble ones of the Lord, who «with groans and sighs, tears and prayers» (Rule 1869, 1, 3°) prepared the coming of the Messiah, the Sisters [and the Brothers] walk humbly with God (cf. Mic 6:8), seeking his face in the secret of their heart and in the fraternal exchange of a communion of prayer that has its center in the Eucharist. In this way, persevering in prayer with Mary, the mother of Jesus, and proclaiming the death and resurrection of the Lord, they prepare with the whole Church his full manifestation: «Come, Lord Jesus!».

Friday

Tr. p. 100, par. 2.4

Struggle in prayer

Jesus awaits our participation for the accomplishment of his redeeming work. What St. Paul says of himself holds for all and always: «I fill up in my flesh what is lacking in Christ's afflictions» (Col 1:24).

It is the part that each of us, individually and as a community, can add to the redeeming work of the Savior. In this sense we can say «already and not yet!».

Since prayer is a gift of such immense value, it is understandable that the devil does everything to prevent or spoil our prayer, whether by disturbing our interior dispositions, or by plotting with «snares» of every kind against our recollection and our silence. Hence the need for vigilance and for diligent preparation of the heart when we set ourselves to pray.

If on our part there is, however, good will, the Holy Spirit will not fail to assist us by driving off the snares of the evil one, who is the enemy of prayer, as he is the enemy of persons, especially of those seriously engaged in the most important work of man on earth: growth in love and in union with God, that is, on the path of holiness.

Saturday

FS pp. 258-259 «She would like to make…November of 1886»

She would like to make of every daughter of St. Anne a spokeswoman of Jesus so as to let all people hear the message of the Love that saves; that all might have the gift she experiences when she feels herself a pure instrument of the One who makes her speak.

She wrote to her intimate Sr. A. Celsa Speranza:

«Jesus will put on your tongue words that you yourself will not know how you pronounced… Love, and think that it was Jesus who spoke in your heart and you were his echo, another» (Letter undated, n. 76).

What matters is, first of all, to evangelize by life (Circ. Letter 20-8-1895). One of the sisters testifies at the informative process: «She wanted and required us to act as missionaries in the hospitals, first by our bearing and then by charity and, finally, by word» (Summ., p. 650).

Two moments of deep joy the apostolic heart of Mother Rosa had: one, when she gave her maternal embrace to the sixteen sisters of the first expedition leaving for Latin America on November 23, 1878, an omen of rapid expansion on that continent; and the other, that day when she presented to Leo XIII the four members of the first mission to East Africa, in November 1886.

28th Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 150-151, «The Church that is … holy and immaculate bride»

The Church, that is, the kingdom of Christ already present in mystery by the power of God, grows visibly in the world. This beginning and this growth are signified by the blood and water that flowed from the opened side of the crucified Christ and are foretold by the Lord's words about his death on the cross: «And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself» (Jn 12:32). Every time the sacrifice of the cross «by which Christ our Paschal Lamb has been sacrificed» (1 Cor 5:7) is celebrated on the altar, the work of our redemption is renewed. And together with the sacrament of the Eucharistic bread, the unity of the faithful, who constitute one body in Christ who is the light of the world, is represented and brought about; from him we come, through him we live, to him we are directed» (LG 3).

In this truly marvelous sense Jesus is our hope and the Church is truly the Ark of the Covenant, prefigured in the old Covenant, divinely realized in the new and eternal Covenant.

The Church is therefore the beginning on earth of the kingdom of Christ and of God.

In the light of this splendid theology of the Church the various images of the Church outlined by the Council are luminously understood: «the Church is a sheepfold whose one and necessary door is Christ; it is a flock of which God himself foretold he would be the shepherd, Christ himself the good Shepherd and prince of shepherds; it is God's field in which the ancient olive tree grows, whose holy root were the patriarchs…; the Church is God's building of which the Lord is the cornerstone, the foundation on which the Church itself is built and from which it will receive stability and cohesion. The Church is the house in which his family dwells, the dwelling of God with men; it is the new Jerusalem, the Holy City. In it, as living stones, we form a spiritual temple. This holy city St. John, in the Apocalypse, contemplates in its final phase, coming down from God as a bride adorned for her husband» (Rev 21:ff.).

The Church is the heavenly Jerusalem, «our mother», the immaculate bride of the immaculate lamb.

And while the Church fulfills on this earth her pilgrimage far from the Lord (cf. 2 Cor 5:6), she is like an exile who seeks and desires the things above, where Christ sits at the right hand of God until with her Spouse she will appear clothed in glory (cf. Col 3:1-4)» (cf. LG 6,7).

Yet the image par excellence is the Church as mystical body formed by Christ and by believers (cf. LG 7).

After this whole series of attributes, the Council also devotes a chapter to the «Church as the people of God». And it is most true, provided one does not forget what it has already said about the «mystical body».

In the heavenly Church the unity of the Church with Christ, in Christ and through Christ will appear more evident, that is, the unity of the Church in the most holy Trinity by the work of the Holy Spirit. The Church, according to the best theologians, is therefore first of all the body of the Lord, the bride of Christ, sacrament of intimate union with God, «Icon» of the most holy Trinity in the image of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, holy and immaculate bride (cf. Eph 5:27).

Monday

Tr. p. 66, «Loving faith…before Abraham was, I am»

Faith: loving adherence to the God of the Covenant, Father, Son, Holy Spirit

Faith makes us believe firmly in the word of God, of which Abraham (Gen 15:6) gave heroic proof, ready for the gravest of sacrifices, fully abandoned to the infinite merciful goodness of God.

No less is the full trusting abandonment to God on the part of Moses on so many occasions during the long, toilsome pilgrimage toward the promised land. His faith is such that it is transformed into full confidence and trust to the point of stopping the threats of God, justly angered by the people's many infidelities. This faith resting wholly on the promise of the future Redeemer constitutes the prelude of Christian faith, not only in Jesus Christ as Messiah, but essentially as God, identical with the Father under the veils of human flesh, as today under the veils of bread and wine.

The key point of Christian faith is therefore to believe in the divinity of Christ proclaimed in the Prologue of his Gospel by John and explicitly confirmed by Jesus himself more than once «before Abraham was, I am» (Jn 8:58).

Tuesday

Tr. pp. 80-81, «In the person of Jesus… in the mystery of the incarnation»

In the person of Jesus the history of the old and new Covenant therefore finds its origin and foundation. Their unity is constituted by Jesus who was to come, Jesus who has come, Jesus who is coming. The old Covenant was prelude and prophecy of what would be revealed and accomplished in the new Covenant personified in Jesus Christ, Son of the Father and Son of Mary, through his examples (Jesus teaches more by deeds than by words) and above all through the full adherence of his will to that of the Father at the supreme moment of accepting passion and death. The old Covenant is then changed into a song of love toward God and neighbor, love practiced and preached by Jesus Christ and already anticipated in many Psalms: «I love you, Lord, my strength» (Ps 18:2); «Love the Lord, all you his saints» (Ps 31:24).

The fundamental law is no different from the one promulgated by Jesus, even if divinely perfected by him: «You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength» (Deut 6:5). It is the work of salvation accomplished by God in view of the merits of Jesus Christ, in whom the long waiting for the One who would be the Savior of all, and of those who would be faithful to the old as to the new Covenant, finds fulfillment and meaning. In the people of God, in fact, some persons are particularly chosen and beloved by him for the special mission he entrusts to them. Among them our gaze rests on the family of Saints Joachim and Anne, parents of Mary, chosen precisely for so high a mission. The supreme example of love of God and neighbor for the charismatic family of Rosa Gattorno is therefore most holy Mary who, being Mother of God, is for that very reason mother of divine Love in its twofold dimension: vertical toward God, and horizontal toward neighbor, on the foundation of the humanity assumed in her by the Word in the mystery of the incarnation.

Wednesday

Tr. pp. 88-89, «In the light of Jesus… the hearts …to make them all the Lord's»

In the light of Jesus, the daughters of St. Anne and those who are called by Christ to imitate this particular attitude of his, choosing the last places, serving, as he himself did, with all gentleness and kindness, and working tirelessly for the extension of the Kingdom, aware that the gifts received are for the common building up, must make their own the words of the Gospel: «When you have done all that you were ordered to do, say: we are worthless slaves. We have done only what we ought to have done» (Lk 17:10), not aspiring to greatness but letting themselves be drawn to what is lowly (cf. Rom 12:16).

Humility, understood in this way, widens the spaces of charity toward God and toward neighbor.

The soul dominated by self-love in all its manifold expressions can neither love God nor serve neighbor. The more sincere and profound humility is, the greater is the charity in which perfection principally consists.

How many times during the day we must pray the Lord to sweep from soul and heart every sentiment of selfishness, praying that he come, that he come ever more effectively to take the place of our ego. Let us not forget to heed the admonition of St. Paul: «What do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as if it were not a gift?» (1 Cor 4:7). The gifts and endowments of nature and grace bestowed by God cannot be denied. What matters, however, is not to boast of them because every endowment and every good comes from him. The gifts received must therefore be welcomed with humble gratitude toward the Giver of every good, because the humble recognition of the truth is the very substance of humility. When this attitude toward God is in the heart, the consciousness of being sinners follows, but together with it the certainty that God saves us. Humility was the fundamental attitude of the Remnant of Israel», and it was, without any doubt, that of Mary's holy parents, and of Mary, who lived it to the highest, exemplary degree, because Immaculate, humble spouse of the just Joseph and mother of Jesus, meek and humble of heart. Therefore the daughters of St. Anne, and all the members of the Family of the holy mother of the Immaculate, regard humility as the foundational virtue of their spirituality as Mother Rosa taught:

«Great prudence, charity, humility, gentleness with everyone… and you will win the hearts of all, to make them all the Lord's» (Letter to Sr. A. Agnese Tacchini, 1900).

Thursday

D. pp. 122-123, par. 3

The Voice Asks for Adherence to God's Plan.

It trains her to walk in step with God, who shows in his interventions that his will is inexhaustible, that the ultimate end toward which he leads her is known only to him, that she cannot content herself with having the certainty of norms approved by human authority. But she must open herself each day to the newness of the Spirit.

Early on she understands through the Voice that God's will sends her to places she could not have imagined. She listens as Abraham did: «Go from your country, your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you» (Gen 12:1), and follows the path indicated by God.

At the moment of deciding to found the Institute in Piacenza, torn by the doubt that what she was living might be an illusion and might not correspond to God's will, in prayer she hears:

«A clear Voice: «All my will what happened, be tranquil, tranquil, everything will be smoothed out»» (M. 2, p. 47).

Rosa loves and adores in silence her God who is revealing himself through the Voice. She finds herself living, perhaps without being aware of it, the experience of Moses who hangs upon the Voice (Ex 3:4) of «He who is» in order to face the risks of the mission, the responsibility (Ex 5:22-23) of guiding and governing a people with a law (Ex 19:20) toward holiness, the concern to give water and nourishment to those who thirst and hunger (Ex 16:17), the unforeseen events of the long and weary wandering (Ex 33:7-17;34 ff). As to Isaiah: «A Voice says: «Cry out»… lift up your voice, do not fear» (Is 40:6-9), and to other prophets the Voice demands to announce the future, to affirm God's will and denounce errors, so to her too it makes known in advance events or calamities so that she may take part in them with her prayer. Through the Voice the Lord communicates to her his love for man:

«A Voice answered me: «Yes, I love man immensely»…». «…You, if one may say so, are mad for man and he? A Voice that says to me: «Yes, I love him dearly» (M. 1.1, p. 152; M. 1.2, p. 1).

Friday

Tr. pp. 130-131, par. 3.2

In the Church, with a specific mission

Choosing Mary Immaculate as their model, they become a sign of hope for the man of today in the preferential action for the poorest, knowing how to identify and relieve the new forms of poverty. They therefore commit themselves to integral liberation in the sense of that freedom with which Christ has set us free (as St. Paul warns). Christ has set us free so that we might remain free: «Stand firm, therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery» (Gal 5:1).

This is the great freedom that sprang from the redeeming death of Christ. An immensely profound freedom that rescues man from the slavery of Satan and of sin, not in the sense restricted to the mere «political» freedom to which the freedom of Christ is sometimes reduced, but in the sense of integral freedom, a prophetic sign of hope for the man of today.

Saturday

TC pp. 521-523, «Always forward…God gave you»

Always forward, never stopping, despite the dictates of human prudence.

Against the expectation of all the workers, I set out and at the first farmhouse where I stopped, after a long journey, I began to have great struggles, because countless were the people who tried to dissuade me, pointing out that this road was held by wrongdoers; every sort of frightening tale they tried to tell me. But no! I clung to the feet of my Crucified and asked him what I should do.

- Forward! - he answered me - Do not fear! So I came to another farmhouse. The snow fell in big flakes, the cold was something horrible; those great valleys and the very high mountains were all covered with snow. At every stretch, a poor man with a donkey helping each other, I would say, for now one fell and now the other: they tried to approach certain farms that could scarcely be made out, being covered with snow. It was picturesque!

After covering many leagues, whenever I met someone, they at once urged me to turn back, because that way was most dangerous and it was not fitting for a creature to venture on it; and when they saw my obstinacy, they tried to seduce the workers who were with me. Having arrived at a certain point, I truly saw certain wrongdoers preparing to start a brawl and it was clearly understood that they had a great desire for blood. Seized by fright, a thousand thoughts crossed my mind: the fear that the workers I had with me might have failed me from fright, and how much a mind disturbed by such horrible events witnessed, and by fantasies, can create. I felt like stopping. I began to pray:

- My Master! must I stop? How can it be that this is your will: that I go further ahead while at every step I advance the wrongdoers increase? Oh! shall I stop?

As I said this, a dear soul of mine, who dwells in the heavenly homeland, appeared and said to me:

- Do not fear: forward! Nothing untoward will happen to you. I shall always be with you.

Full of vigor, encouraged by so great a saint, I ran swiftly on my path and, crossing countless fields and sea, at last I arrived happily where my Lord commanded me.

How to express the joy of the workers who came to meet me? Among the many there was one whose (countenance) stood out in a singular way. Who was she? A great lady who for years has worked in the Lord's fields in an extraordinary way: my beloved, tireless for the greater glory of God. She, invested with a sublime spirit, as always was a great relief to me in everything! Like a matron, distinguished by her noble qualities, she always keeps a heart so charitable and a spirit upright and sincere. Oh! sublime woman, who think only of relieving the wretched! This slave, generously benefited by you, looks upon your merits and your great virtues. Great knowledge God gave you!

29th Sunday in Ordinary Time

FS pp. 78-79, par. 4

Mother Rosa, teacher of prayer.

From the first day of the foundation she organized the novitiate of Piacenza with an intense schedule of prayer life and, therefore, in an atmosphere of retreat. She herself directed the morning meditation, generally on the Passion of Christ, with accents full of unction, in order to set the young religious on the path of mental prayer. In her instructions to the novices she gave primary importance to contemplative prayer. But the most effective lesson was herself, her example, her hours of contemplation, her habitual absorption in God, as well as her words full of fervor and higher light, that gentle and penetrating gaze of hers that silently called one to account, and the whole bearing of one who breathes the atmosphere of the divine. She was for all the best stimulus to commit themselves seriously on the paths of the search for God.

From the brief recommendations we find in her letters to the sisters we can deduce what the exhortations were that she made by word of mouth, in personal conversations and in conferences, especially on the occasion of visits:

«Prayer is our only shield of defense» - «It is the key to graces» - «Do not forget to be always in the presence of God the Father; remember the instructions this wretched one gave you» - «Ah! what happiness to be united with the good God! But you, my dear, if you stay far from this most loving Spouse, what will you ever have? nothing. Go, go and suck the honey of sweetness; He is its essence, so run to his fountain and drink, get drunk!…» (to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 5-12-1868, 18-9-1869, 16-1-1870, 14-11-1873; to Sr. A. Vincenza Rapallino: 3-12-1872).

In a special way she recommended attention and fidelity to God's inspirations, which requires the spirit of prayer that disposes one to listen to the divine calls.

«Woe to that creature who has made herself deaf to the inspirations that God, in his mercy, gives her» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 21-12-1868).

Monday

TC pp. 397-398 «Now let us take a look… my voice tells me»

- Now let us take a look at the fine work my Master did. Not only did he dispel everything, but he made use of the evil to draw from it a fertilizer for his fields, and we see them beautiful and vigorous. The trees put forth their foliage, the vines their delightful leaves, the pines and oaks are full of graceful birds' nests that with their song weave graceful melodies. Whoever has the good fortune to rest in the shade of these delightful plants enjoys peace and consolation from them.

She looks at me and, smiling, thanks me, and tries to work well and willingly. I put her to work and see to it that it is the lightest and least disastrous. So together we worked, when night overtook us without our noticing. She, almost frightened, said to me:

- What are we doing here in the middle of this field? Only work is spoken of and never do we try to sustain ourselves. I answered her:

- Do not doubt, for my Master is that God who feeds the birds, and who can fear not having what he needs? (cf. Mt 6:26).

I look around and see nothing. The field was without trees, not even a farm was in sight. My God! what will happen to this poor creature if she is not provided with what is necessary? Teach me what I must do.

- Trust, and nothing else - my voice tells me.

Tuesday

Tr. pp. 95-96, «When one truly loves… knowledge of the Gospel «

When one truly loves the Lord, when one thinks that he is more intimate to us than we are to ourselves, one ends by making of one's whole life a dialogue of intimacy; of filial abandonment to the Father, in full adherence to the divine will, with total offering of oneself in every daily circumstance, in uninterrupted union with Jesus in the Eucharist; of docility to the Holy Spirit; of total surrender to the most holy Trinity; of tenderness toward most holy Mary, our sweetest mother; and of love and filial trust in St. Anne, the angels and the saints, just as Mother Rosa did.

An unsurpassable model of prayer remains for us the one taught by Jesus himself: «Our Father who art in heaven», which contains the truth of our sonship and daughterhood before God creator, redeemer, sanctifier, and for that very reason opens us also to the experience of universal brotherhood with all the members of the human community who, thanks to the mystery of the incarnation, become a single family in Christ in the communion and sharing of the material and spiritual goods generously bestowed on all by the infinite goodness of God.

All the members of the human family either are Christians or have the vocation to know and love Jesus Christ. With him, in him and through him we can call our God «Father».

Hence the urgency of missionary and evangelizing activity so that the «virtual» call may become actual and explicit through knowledge of the Gospel.

Wednesday

Tr. pp. 96-97, «While he was teaching…all people»

While he was teaching the «Our Father» Jesus was surrounded by his disciples. Still today he continues to be present among those who pray with faith. The scene of Jesus praying to the Father with his disciples has therefore become the paradigm of Christian prayer. When the Christian, consecrated persons, the whole Church, and in her all the members of the Family of the holy Mother, take up an attitude of prayer, Jesus prays with them, and they pray with the divine Master.

But Christian prayer does not consist only in what Jesus teaches: the Our Father. The prayer of Christian prayers is in fact the sacrifice of the Mass, which is at once adoration, praise, thanksgiving, reparation, petition, expiation. The deepest adoration coincides with the very sacrifice of the altar: the priest is identical: Jesus; the victim is identical: Jesus! Our most lovable redeemer, who is still Jesus, continues to be the Master of our prayer, not in words, but in deeds, with his eternal, universal sacrifice, of infinite impetratory value, source of all justice.

Our prayer therefore acquires value to the extent that it shares in the prayer-sacrifice of the Lord.

Since the sacrifice of the altar, the unbloody continuation of the sacrifice of the cross, is the model of our prayer, only by praying with Jesus do we become sharers in the redemption of the world, following the example of most holy Mary who, by taking part in the prayer and in the mystery of the redemption of the Son, became the Mediatrix and the Mother of all people.

Thursday

TC pp. 487-488, «Oh! I exclaimed aloud…with superhuman strength I ran»

Oh! - I exclaimed aloud - here I am alone! and where am I going? My voice:

- Behind the light that guides you!

I already felt myself failing, but I did not want to stop, because the light so indicated. Meanwhile it seemed to me from moment to moment that I would fall to the ground and I prayed my Lord to send me my angel, because I felt myself failing. Behold, the light no longer marks the path, but forms itself all around me; I stop and it surrounds me as if it had enclosed me in itself. I was near a graceful stone. I sat down; I felt myself strengthened, I gathered a little strength; but the long fast, the weariness, all that I had gone through (kept me worn out).

I was praying and waiting for I know not what: human relief certainly could not be had; but I do not know. I knew nothing, neither what to think nor how I should hope for comfort. Wrapped in that light and seated I prayed. From the light itself came a graceful hand with a glass, and a voice that said to me: - Drink and you will be satisfied.

I drank. The light opened again and marked the path. And I, with superhuman strength, ran.

Friday

Tr. pp. 142-144, par. 1.4

The person docile to the action of grace reaches the full maturity of Christ as child in the Son

Docility to the action of the Spirit makes us new creatures, transformed in the image of Christ Jesus and ever more aware of living in him, through him and with him the inheritance he acquired for us by offering himself as victim of the new Covenant.

The Father himself illumines this reality of ours through his Word: «The Holy Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are children of God. And if children, then heirs, heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if only we suffer with him so that we may also be glorified with him. I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory about to be revealed to us» (Rom 8:16-18).

Having, then, to share in Christ's suffering, and the Father knowing our weakness, he does not leave us alone in the effort of identification with the firstborn Son of every man.

«The Spirit helps us in our weakness; for we do not know how to pray as we ought, but that very Spirit intercedes with sighs too deep for words. And God, who searches hearts, knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints according to the will of God. We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, who are called according to his purpose. For those whom he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, in order that he might be the firstborn within a large family. And those whom he predestined he also glorified» (Rom 8:28-30).

Mother Rosa believed firmly in God's plan, and so she did not spare her life, always hoping, even against all hope, in him, her Good, her strength and her defender: «Who will accuse the elect of God? It is God who justifies. Who will condemn? Christ Jesus who died, or rather, who was raised, is at the right hand of God and intercedes for us. Who will separate us, then, from the love of Christ? Will tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or the sword?

As it is written: for your sake we are being put to death all day long, we are regarded as sheep to be slaughtered.

No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us».

This same certainty must grow in us so that we may experience in life, in total surrender to the Father, how «neither death, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord» (Rom 8:38-39).

To be children in the Son is our destiny, but it is still the object of our hope. «In hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope; for who hopes for what one already sees? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with perseverance» (Rom 8:24-25).

Saturday

D. pp. 81-82, «The promise of Jesus… live in love»

The Promise of Jesus Is Fulfilled.

These ineffable moments nourish an ever higher perception of the Presence that Jesus promised for the soul that loves him.

Rosa is one of these souls who, loving him, merits the fulfillment of Jesus' promise:

«Oh! my Love, what you make me feel in this your Heart. Oh! if man could come to understand the greatness one feels in this Love, surely he would not hesitate a minute to put away those affections that soon wither.

Only your Love increases every day and I shall say better it never ends» (M. 1.1, p.46).

She discovers that the secret of having her Good present is to associate herself with his redeeming mystery, and so she comes to full acceptance of suffering:

«While I was in the fierce persecutions, behold my God who comes to comfort me. What to do but wish that others would soon come, because thus my Good came to comfort me? Oh! your caresses!…»

«Tribulations, sorrows rained upon me from every side. But how to feel them, nothing! In my love everything remains absorbed by the sweetness of his Love. Yes, beat, for this donkey is hard and my soul rejoices greatly. An indescribable calm. Last night as I was about to take my usual rest on the cross I felt myself rapt» (M. 1.1, p. 117; 157).

Through her dedication she can feel addressed to herself the words of God: «I will betroth you to me in faithfulness» (Hos 2:22). Her faith becomes, in fact, ever more fidelity, adherence to God's will. Such adherence is all the more solid in that, within the soul, her Good testifies to his own presence through a light that is participation in the divine light. Rosa therefore walks the path of sanctification willed by him, following the light.

Out of love she unites herself to her most holy God, and for that very reason is bound to become holy, but since God is love, she understands that she must live in love.

30th Sunday in Ordinary Time

TC pp. 124-125, «I walked for long hours… my happiness»

I walked for long hours without trouble, and so beautiful and graceful a creation was pleasing to me, both to the eye and even to the heart. There was a moment when I took delight in it and, without realizing it, let my natural feeling feed on that delightful sight. Walking thus, I met a shepherd and he asked me where I was heading.

- I do not know!

- Are you sure you are walking well?

- Most sure!

- Do you not fear meeting people who could trouble you?

- No!

And he joined me. He told me many things about the duties of submission we have, and how much souls gain when they are guided in everything by their suffering: they have a hundred percent gain. Meanwhile I kept looking at the dear and beautiful delights of the plain, without minding that I was accompanied. I gave a deep sigh:

- How beautiful you are, O valleys and delightful hills, bushes gilded by the reflection of the sun, clusters of lilies!

And I stopped.

- A gloom overtakes me: I can reason no more. Only my God, who created you, and surely serves him better than I, and graciously adorns his earth… I, alas!

And I made a loud lament, without noticing that a shepherd was with me; and I hurried on, running like one who seeks to rid herself of an unbearable weight. The poor shepherd stops me, begging me to go more slowly, and to make use of him if I had anything that grieved me, for he would have relieved me in everything. With a gesture of surprise (I said to him):

- What? you still here? I need nothing: One alone I seek, but I do not find him; He alone is all my happiness.

Monday

D. pp. 108-109, par. 4

The Spirit Paraclete (the One who is called alongside), sent by Jesus to all people to move them to love with all their heart, with all their soul and with all their strength, who also comes to convict «the world in regard to sin» (Jn 16:8), is Rosa's interior teacher.

She points out, in her Memoirs, that the Spirit guides her, enlightens her and purifies her on the path of sanctification:

«Oh, my Love! I was enraptured in him: what I saw, what I felt…! He showed me certain imperfections; although I know myself to be a heap of infamy, yet in that union, my Good, washes my poor soul which remains purified in the fire of his divine Love. Oh! sweetness…» (M. 1.2, p. 118).

On another page, describing the union with her God, she adds:

«…I was so convinced of my nothingness… that it seemed I no longer had the courage to stand in the presence of my God…, the more intimate the union became, the more I discovered my nothingness…»;

«…I was afflicted because I had no one to whom to say a word. A Voice said to me: «why do you say this? do you not remember what I told you a short time before such a defeat reached you from Rome? I am your Master, be at peace. The peace of conscience that I enjoy in the midst of so many tribulations… is such that I see there is a most powerful Spirit who governs me…» (M. 3, p. 21; M. 4.1, p. 4).

Rosa is conformed to Christ by this Presence dwelling in her, who animates her, sustains her, goes before her and accompanies her in the fulfilment of her vocation to holiness.

Tuesday

FS pp. 224-225, «The Foundress… in his Church «

The foundress had to suffer setbacks, misunderstandings, even harsh humiliations, which more than once put her unshakeable trust in the hierarchical Church to a hard test. This is how she expresses herself, in her metaphorical language:

«The boat tied up well, as best I knew how, I sought to carry myself to my Good in his great temple, to his Vicar. Oh! what a surprise! Ill-clad, ragged as I was, a poor slave of the Lord, I kissed the foot and the hand of his Vicar. O most humble sovereign!

O mercy of God! The Vicar asks me about the little ship, wishes it near him and prophesies the future to me. O my Saviour! with what vigour I had run to take the little boat to bring it where the Vicar wished! But a stormy sea rises, a contrary wind rages and dashes me against a rock… After a short struggle my little ship came out more beautiful… Brought to the feet of Peter, I knew how to say nothing else to him except that he should say many things for me to my God: that I was bringing the little boat to the feet of his Vicar, so that it might be incorporated into his Church» (TC, pp. 218-220).

Wednesday

TC pp. 131-134, «By which side shall I pass…I am always near you»

By which side shall I pass to reach this field? There is no road. These two old people tried to console me and told me many things, all about the life of my Lord; but while they would have liked me to take part in them, they did not notice that I felt deep and vivid sorrow: the sufferings of my God caused me such pain that I burst into a flood of tears. And they were convinced that I loved my Lord very much. The old woman took me by the hand and, raising me up graciously, showed me the field. And I added:

- And the way to go there, where is it found?

Suddenly I notice that a servant of God, who died in the reputation of holiness, is near me (who says to me):

- Here is the road!

- I, set foot on so disastrous a road? And how to have the courage to ask the one you tell me I shall find, who will give me the exact outline of the journey I must make?

Having said this, he answered me that I should not hold back any more, but obey, for it is the will of God. I fell silent and set out at the beginning of a long road. I see a shepherd, and at once I asked him to give me the map of the land I had to cross, for this was the will of my God and out of obedience I played this part, and I did so in complete mortification. He looked at me, and then answered that he would give it to me very soon. And so, calmly, I waited for it. When a gentle lady hands me, by order of that shepherd, the outline of the road I had to travel.

Without answering further I set out and, along the way, I was very mortified, because I had not prayed at all for that dear lady who had come with me; I was not a little grieved. Reasoning thus I see that on this road there was nothing but bushes and uncultivated plants. But where, my God, is the beautiful field you promised me? Nothing! I began to weep and to make a loud lament, because I was tired and night was drawing near; nothing else was heard but the howls of wild beasts. What torment is this? I went on reasoning and running. When the night is far advanced, a shepherd appears before me, all ill-clad, who stops me, snatching from my hand the outline that lady had given me, and roughly abuses me and, mocking me, leaves me. What to do? where to take shelter? Almost lost I threw myself face down on the ground and implored the Most High to come to my aid. A voice:

- What? do you lose yourself for so little?

With a rush I rose and, running, reached a very large estate, where a man of God lived, and running to his feet I begged for pity and mercy. Such was the welcome of that angel, more than man! Having heard my reasons and seeing me so battered, the other did nothing but pity me and encourage me, telling me that I would soon have my new outline, and that he blessed my journey which was very pleasing to God. I took heart and asked him whether it was really true that my Lord, in such terrible struggles of mine, is satisfied and approves the continual torment of this journey of mine.

- Very much! - he answered me, and that I should not doubt that he would keep his gaze continually upon me.

I began to tell him that I am always alone, because he left me so, and that he should tell him that I always desire him near. He assured me he would do everything. And dismissed me. Oh! what was my joy!

I was not slow to be troubled and become sad, because I had indeed met a harsh shepherd who ordered me to stop running, since for me there is now no road to reach that field I had set out to travel. What to do? My voice:

- Run! and do not trouble yourself, because I am always near you.

Thursday

D. p. 69, «Infinite Wisdom… drew near me»

Infinite Wisdom makes her a sharer in his Light which penetrates the hearts of people, searches them, shakes them, converts them:

«He let me see into certain hearts and said this to me: every time it happens that you wish to see and penetrate them, you will see them. So whatever you ask of me for the good of the souls who are with you and of whom you have the care, I shall give you everything. So too for what you desire for Priests, the very thing you wish me to give them through prayer, I shall give them. You will distinguish clearly the good from the bad; I shall make you feel an abhorrence when they have indecent ideas against chastity. You will feel it at once and be warned. Do not doubt that I shall always be near you, there are many… Oh! what pain… I felt. So for the false devout women you will have special lights to distinguish well…» (M. 1.1, p. 63).

She receives most beautiful instructions on the love Jesus has for man, while man responds poorly:

«Oh! my Beloved! Oh! Yes, I see well how much you love creatures, and they respond to you so poorly. You are all love for them! A Voice answered me, yes I love man immensely, and while he was saying this to me he drew near me» (M. 1.1, p. 152).

Friday

Tr. pp. 84-86, par. 1.5

Simplicity and prudence form an inseparable pair.

The chosen people knew the importance of letting themselves be guided prudently by God, by wisdom (cf. Wis 9:11); in doubt over a choice they were accustomed to respect the supreme dominion of God: «To God belong counsel and prudence» (Job 12:13). From generation to generation the faithful learned: «Learn prudence, you simple ones» (Prov 8:5); «wisdom teaches temperance and prudence» (Bar 9ff.).

In this school St. Anne and Mary her daughter had been educated, enlightened by that prudence which Jesus, as Master, will teach to all humanity.

When he sends his disciples to proclaim the Gospel he indeed warns them: «I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; so be shrewd as serpents and simple as doves» (Mt 10:16).

Jesus' warning continues to hold all its value today, as it did in the time of Mother Rosa, who lived applying to all her choices the criteria of this virtue without separating it from simplicity.

«Prudence is that light which between two things makes you always choose the one that best leads you to gain and to increase the love of God» (Reg. 1869, p. 25).

No virtue stands, therefore, without prudence. The Christian and also pre-Christian moral tradition define prudence, in fact, as the virtue of virtues, the virtue that guides and directs all the others.

Saturday

Tr. pp. 88, «In the light… every good comes from Him»

In the light of Jesus, the daughters of St. Anne and those who are called by Christ to imitate this particular attitude of his, choosing the last places, serving, as he himself did, with all gentleness and kindness, and working tirelessly for the extension of the Kingdom, aware that the gifts received are for the common edification, must make their own the words of the Gospel: «When you have done all that you were commanded, say: we are unprofitable servants. We have done what we ought to have done» (Lk 17:10), not aspiring to greatness but letting themselves be drawn by what is lowly (cf. Rom 12:16).

Humility, understood in this way, widens the spaces of charity towards God and towards neighbour.

The soul dominated by self-love in all its manifold expressions can neither love God nor serve neighbour. The more sincere and profound humility is, the greater is the charity in which perfection principally consists.

How many times during the day must we ask the Lord to sweep from soul and heart every feeling of selfishness, praying that he come, that he come ever more effectively to take the place of our ego. Let us not forget to heed the admonition of St. Paul: «What do you possess that you have not received? And if you received it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?» (1 Cor 4:7). The gifts and endowments of nature and of grace bestowed by God cannot be denied. What matters, however, is not to boast of them, because every endowment and every good comes from Him.

31st Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 78-79, «The whole history…her mystical writings»

The whole history of the old and the new Covenant is centred on the divine person of Jesus, Son of God and Son of man, that is, son of the Virgin Mary, the Immaculate.

At the foundation of the history of salvation there is therefore God's love for the human person.

Creation and redemption are thus realities traceable to the love God has for the human creature, the first origin of all history, which finds in the incarnate Word its deepest meaning and its root.

In him and through him everything is explained and everything finds its reason and its one meeting point. One understands well, then, the sense of the words in the great prayer of Jesus: «Holy Father, keep in unity all those you have given me, that they also may be one, as you Father in me and I in you… so that the world may believe that you sent me. And the glory you gave me I have given to them, that they may be one as we are one» (Jn 17:20-21). Here is the way of Christian perfection and holiness: to become one with Jesus, to identify oneself progressively with him, in order to become one with the Father and the Holy Spirit. The way to attain such unity was lived and taught by Mother Rosa, eager to become one with Christ crucified.

To fulfil hope is, then, to set it within love for the Crucified. From this derives the living and perennial relevance of Mother Rosa's charism, who could well say with St. Paul: «I resolved to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ and him crucified» (1 Cor 2:2).

This was also Mother Rosa's wisdom (especially mystical). But this wisdom is nothing other than ardent love for Jesus and particularly for Jesus crucified, as can easily be deduced from the facts of her life and from her mystical writings.

Monday

TC pp. 363-365… «I would never have departed… love for his creatures»

I would never have departed from this temple; but it was his will that I leave it. So, without further remark, I set out. After two hours and more of walking, behold what the voice had told me. Oh magnificence! it was something delightful. I entered fields of varied and diverse flowers; many graceful young girls vied to offer them to me. I accepted many; but I always kept in mind the word: «You will find flowers and laurel to weave». What am I to do? - I kept saying to myself. And these kept bringing me more and more. There was laurel. One of them, older and bold, said to me:

- See all these fields, how beautiful they are and so full of flowers!

- Yes - I answered her.

- Well, since we do not know how to weave them, once gathered they wither and become foul-smelling.

- Oh! - I added - Why do you not try to give them to Jesus?

- Tell us how we should do it.

- Let us make a garland and give it to that church which has a field attached, but a poor one; the farmhouse where the poor workers are is so dilapidated that those poor women live there wretchedly.

These creatures were listening to me.

- Well then! - they said to me - weave as many as you wish, take them to those creatures, and also for the church you speak of.

I was not slow to set to work. And they helped me with great pleasure. How happy I felt, because I was doing great things with those bouquets. I took a quantity of laurel.

- This - I said - is for you, who with such generosity help the poor and the spouses of the Lord, as well as his church. You will be crowned with laurel for an eternity. And I shall strive to weave it so well, putting into it all the skill my Master will give me.

One of these, who more than the others remained silent, comes up to me and says:

- Could I not also learn together with you the same lessons that your Master gives you?

- Oh! yes, certainly! He - I began to say - is all for all, and greatly rejoices when a creature shows herself eager to learn. Yes, come with me and you will see how you will learn to weave roses and lilies… I was forgetting the laurel: more than anything Jesus my own cares about this, and how graceful is his garland!

Without thinking, carried away by joy, I exclaimed: My Love! My Love! Enchanted, she said to me:

- But how, since you have told us already that you are alone and a slave of the Lord.

- And it is true what you say - I answered her - Is he not my God, my Love?

- What? - this one resumed, as if I had blasphemed - you speak of love?

- Yes, my God is all love for his creatures.

Tuesday

Tr. pp. 142-144, par. 1.4

Docility to the action of the Spirit makes us new creatures, transformed into the image of Christ Jesus and ever more aware of living in him, through him and with him the inheritance he won for us by offering himself as victim of the new Covenant.

The Father himself illumines this reality of ours through his Word: «The Holy Spirit bears witness to our spirit that we are children of God. And if we are children, we are also heirs, heirs of God, co-heirs with Christ, if indeed we share in his sufferings, so as to share also in his glory. For I consider that the sufferings of the present time are not worth comparing with the glory to be revealed to us» (Rom 8:16-18).

Since we must, then, share in the suffering of Christ, the Father, who knows our weakness, does not leave us alone in the effort of identification with the firstborn Son of every man.

«The Spirit comes to the aid of our weakness, for we do not know how to pray as we ought, but the Spirit himself intercedes insistently for us with inexpressible groanings. And he who searches hearts knows what is the intention of the Spirit, because he intercedes for the believers according to the will of God. We know that all things work for good for those who love God, who are called according to his purpose. For those he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that he might be the firstborn among many brothers; and those he predestined he also glorified» (Rom 8:28-30).

Mother Rosa firmly believed in God's design, and for this she did not spare her life, always hoping, even against all hope, in him, her Good, her fortress and her defender: «Who will bring a charge against God's chosen ones? God is the one who acquits. Who will condemn? Christ Jesus who died, rather, who was raised, who is at the right hand of God, who indeed intercedes for us. What will separate us, then, from the love of Christ? Will anguish, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or the sword?

As it is written: for your sake we are being slain all day long; we are counted as sheep to be slaughtered.

No, in all these things we conquer overwhelmingly through him who loved us».

This same certainty must grow in us, so that we may experience in life, in total surrender to the Father, how «neither death, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord» (Rom 8:38-39).

To be children in the Son is our destiny, but it is still the object of our hope. «In hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope; for who hopes for what he sees? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with perseverance» (Rom 8:24-25).

Wednesday

FS pp. 161-162, «The important point… is borne with love»

The important point, and not an easy one, is to keep interior peace and joy of heart unaltered under the weight of the cross (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 1867, 26-5-1873). To succeed in this disposition a good dose of patience and much faith are needed:

«Come, courage! Soon you will see that the Lord will console you; but an ounce of patience and two of faith in God, and you will have everything, I assure you. But peace, and little sophistry; day by day embrace the cross the Lord sends us; remember that new days bring new crosses» (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 12-8-1870).

It will not always be easy to be cheerful amid the anguish that oppresses us; then, at least resignation is needed, not the passive kind that makes a virtue of necessity, but that which consists in courageous conformity to the will of God (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 4-11-1869, 20-10-1871; to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 23-3-1871).

«Courage! resignation! May they be our two shields that sustain us in all the immense vicissitudes found in the Lord's Work» (Letter to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti: 8-6-1872). But the secret of suffering well lies in loving well. Love changes the harshness of pains into sweetness and gentleness.

«How sweet it is to love God in suffering!» (Letter to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 5-2-1872).

Everything must be accepted from God out of love, everything must be offered to Him with love, from Him alone must the reward be awaited, never from men, in Him alone must comfort be sought. With the gaze on the Saviour in agony on the cross and on the Sorrowful Mother, every torment is accepted and borne with love (Letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa: 2-12-1868, 1-7-1869, 27-9-1870; to Sr. A. Adelaide Pezzoni: 26-3-1871; to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti: 29-10-1873).

Thursday

TC pp. 302-305, «I set out on my path…acknowledge her fault»

I set out on my path and, along it, I went thinking of the greatness of God and his infinite mercy. Meanwhile I stop for a moment and, kneeling on the ground, with my forehead on a stone (I pray):

- From your mercy I want love! I am exhausted, but I desire nothing but love!

My voice:

- It is not a time for sweetness, but for sufferings! Carry yourself along this road.

I rose and, running, continued:

- My Love, in suffering there is love!

And breathless I regained strength:

- But from your love, my Master, I receive it!

What a sight! As I drew near to where I heard cries and laments, I felt my breast being torn. What can it be? There was still a considerable distance, but the keeper of that field saw me from afar and ran to meet me. We were so breathless and panting, one to hear and the other to tell, that we stopped without being able to exchange a word.

- Oh! - she resumed - Blessed be God who brought you here! There are a great many dissensions, to the point that some want to abandon our field. The very owners, who gave it to us, are also angry with us. Come to our aid, for pity's sake!

- Do not fear, for the Lord will put everything right.

I ran. Directed to the place, behold a crowd of people, but the worst were the workers who, imprudently, without realizing it, were doing great harm. These withdrawn and the master heard, my voice:

- All the damage is because of that worker who stays silently withdrawn: think about it.

When I had finished setting everything in order, without the master and the others noticing, I took her away. My God! how terrible hypocrisy is and how cunningly it knows how to act! She was one of the most zealous and silent, so much that the keeper confided in her: she was good for her, because she used her for her own ends, wickedly; and she would have utterly destroyed that field for her.

But along the way she broke her silence and, with insulting words, threatened me if I did not take her back there. With what force I urged her to calm down and come with me, that God would see to settling all her accounts, which she said she had left in that field. Seeing herself now far away and no longer able to hope to return there, oh! how she went beyond all reason! With how much gentleness I could try (I tried) to persuade her: nothing! She threw her garments on the ground and, clothed in some rag or other, went back to where she had no more peace.

Thus distressed I threw myself at the feet of my Crucified and, holding him to my breast, I commended that soul to him, and with tears of deep sorrow I made a lament:

- Why did it happen so? Along the way I begged you to give strength to my words, that she might be converted: why let her be lost?

I could get nothing in reply. Tired, at the foot of the cross I fell asleep. In a dream I saw a creature whom God had so greatly benefited; she took no account of what she received, but attributed to herself all she had. I said to my God: This soul will not know what she is doing. Poor thing, it grieves me; surely, inwardly she is innocent. Another person steps forward, whom I could not make out, and says:

Anything but innocent! look! And vanished.

As if in a painted picture, her evil inclinations could be seen, and everything derived from pride; her heart, eager to have a response to her affections of flattery, was so black and ill-joined…; only the swollen valve could be seen; smoke came out of her nostrils; her ears had a horn on each side; on her forehead she wore a bandage black as coal; from her mouth came certain flames of fire. Alas! at such a sight, all frightened I threw myself on the ground: Miserere mei, Deus! Have pity, my God! To what a state is that poor soul reduced! Ah! grant me, I beg you, my God, to suffer as much as you wish provided I obtain that she leave sin and return to humility and acknowledge her fault.

Friday

TC pp. 487-490, «Oh!- I cried aloud…will be relieved»

Oh! - I cried aloud - here I am alone! and where am I going? My voice:

- Behind the light that guides you!

I already felt faint, but I did not want to stop, because the light so indicated. Meanwhile it seemed to me from moment to moment that I would fall to the ground and I prayed my Lord to send me my angel, because I felt faint. Behold the light no longer shows the road, but becomes all around me; I stop and it surrounds me as if it had enclosed me in itself. I was near a graceful stone. I sat down; I felt myself revive, I gathered a little strength; but the long fast, the weariness, all that I had gone through (kept me prostrate).

I was praying and waiting for I know not what: human refreshment certainly could not be had; but I do not know. I knew nothing, neither how to think nor how I should await comfort. Wrapped in that light and seated, I prayed. From the same light came a graceful hand with a cup, and a voice that said to me: - Drink and you will be satisfied.

I drank. The light opened again and showed the road. And I, with superhuman strength, ran. Meanwhile it could be perceived a little that dawn would soon come. My mind went over all that had happened. A poor soul, who a few hours before had passed into eternity, whispered to me asking for prayers. So I thought to satisfy her wish; I would have wanted other signs from her, but in vain.

- But why do you always trouble me to have from me… - so the sentence remained suspended, because my voice (interrupted me):

- What you desire you shall have, but there is still time.

She prays. Oh! dear soul, dear to God, blessed by my Lord for ever! But other souls present themselves to me in the act of supplication. Oh! dear friends, what can I do for you? I am a poor slave and worse: yes, for from time to time I serve my Master badly. I still feel the pain of a negligence committed: I was running carelessly, and where did I find myself? This conversation took place along my way.

- And now, dear friends, see: I must walk, but I know neither where nor how I shall find a place to stop.

One answered me:

- It is very long, but it is very dear to God. Ah! offer for us a portion of these labours, so that we may soon be freed from so many sufferings.

I answered at once:

- Not a portion, but all this little that I am walking!

Oh! I hear a deep voice:

- And for me nothing? For so many years I have been condemned to darkness and only from you can I have light.

My God! this voice is not new to me. Oh! that soul!… Ah! may I see her. Behold she is there: how she suffered! And what to do? The labour of that journey was offered by those; I felt deep pain at not being able to give this one at once some relief. Oh! the charity of the just soul! Both souls whom I wanted to benefit present themselves ready before me:

- Your suffering is too great; it is right that that soul have a portion of what you wished to do for us and become a sharer in the offering: most willingly we cede the right.

- Oh charity! Thank you, dear friends! and I promise you that I shall redouble my care until I have the fortune to see you yourselves in the heavenly homeland.

Oh! how I felt true consolation!

- Well then, you burn to be able soon to come to enjoy Him who forms all my longing, my only treasure, sweetest Master. Believe me, as much as you I feel what you feel of sorrow and pain, an inconceivable ardour to reach Him. Oh! once you have arrived at my God, tell him that I desire soon what I have asked of him for so long. Ah! speak to him of me, and then remember to come.

They come close to me, and one says to me:

- For me there will still be much; I suffer much: look at my pains!

Alas! a trembling seized me… Oh most merciful Saviour! tell me what you want me to do for this poor soul: I offer myself to you to expiate her pains. My voice:

- Only in part do I permit it to you, because the journey is long and worse than what you suffer now you will have to suffer on arrival. I was agitated; but the sight of those pains was before me and I had a vivid desire to relieve her. Well then, my Lord, be it only in part, but at least she will be relieved.

Saturday

TC pp. 222-225, «It will never be… make me leave my Lord»

It will never be that all the riches down here make me leave my Lord.

I rose to run, but the wounds on my legs and body were a source of great trouble. I entered a beautiful field, but very poorly cultivated; a graceful peasant woman came to meet me and asked what was the matter with me. Oh! I almost did not want to say it, but she added again:

«Are you feeling unwell?» «No!»

Only at her insistence did I tell her that I had certain wounds on my legs and feet, which did not let me walk. She looked at me with compassion.

«Come into my little country house; I have a certain ointment that will heal you.»

I looked at her, and then gave another glance at my path, which was in no way directed to the little country house.

«Thank you! May God repay your charity, but I cannot stop.»

And I continued on my way. At last, having come near a stream, I sat down and meanwhile bathed the wounds in that water. It came suddenly to my mind: Oh! my Crucified did not have this refreshment for his countless wounds, and am I to have it for this single portion? I left this refreshment at once, and walked on. Those wounds which I had bathed and which burned me less I immediately sought to aggravate with stinging herbs. And I always asked pardon of my God.

I passed near a garden, magnificent for its flowers, graceful in its design; on all sides beautiful coats of arms were seen and from time to time a guard. My path was directed precisely to one of these. Hardly had I entered when I found myself lost in so much wealth of trees and fruits.

A guard comes to meet me and brusquely tells me where I am going, and that I should not be long in leaving, because wandering persons could not enter there. What to do? I tried to persuade him, but there was no reason to convince him. My path was that one and I could not leave it.

«In the name of my Lord, let me pass!»

«No! go back!»

Then I said to him:

«It will never be that I do this, because I have orders to come this way.

«Who are you?» he asked me.

I am a slave of the Lord who sent me here.

While the dispute went on, I commended myself to my God that he turn my path aside. No! A great Lady arrives, all dressed in brocade; with her she had a large dog; and meanwhile she comes up to me and tells me to go back, making a sign of using violence and driving me out. My Crucified! you were thus driven out by Annas!

«Let me go on! I promise not to damage anything, but quickly to pass.»

«No!»

They set the dog on me to drive me out. Nothing! the animal does not move. The woman wanted to give me alms and told me that she felt great compassion.

«Thank you! I do not need alms, because my Lord is very rich and lets me lack nothing. Ah! let me pass!»

Moved to compassion, she looked at me from head to foot and then asked me to sit down, for she wanted to speak to me.

«Your charity and kindness in all that you ask of me would deserve my condescension, but I cannot: night is advancing and I must withdraw.

With a compassionate act she gave me leave to pass, telling the guard to accompany me. Suddenly I find her again near me:

«Stop!»

«No!»

«If you stop with me I assure you I shall make you happy. Do you see?»

«It will never be that all the riches and beauties down here make me leave my Lord.»

32nd Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 128-130, par. 3.1

The daughters of St. Anne, and the other members of the Family, in waiting for the Lord who comes, build the kingdom in poverty of heart and maternal and paternal self-giving.

Acting in the Church according to a specific mission, they collaborate in Christ's saving work, bearing in their hearts a single passion: the Kingdom of God and the glory of the Father, following the example of the foundress.

They are therefore committed to the increase of holy faith, the conversion of sinners and the service of their brothers and sisters, made a sign and instrument of the merciful love of the Father for all people. Inserted in the reality of the local Church, they are a leaven of communion, witnesses of hope and a presence of proclamation, and they build the kingdom in poverty of heart and maternal and paternal self-giving.

As St. Anne awaited the fulfilment of the promises, the one sent by the Father, so they too, while awaiting the glorious manifestation of the Lord, burning with zeal like Mother Rosa, are committed to making him known to the whole world in the certainty that God has worked, works and will continue to work great things in persons thanks to prayer and to our industrious apostolic activity, even when the cross of Jesus, physical or spiritual, invites us to travel, at least in part, the road of Calvary.
