And the cross and the Crucified whom Mother Rosa loved with such ardour and generous devotion, just as the Psalm says: «Lord, my rock and my fortress, my deliverer, my God, my rock of refuge, my shield and my stronghold, my mighty salvation. The waves of death surrounded me, torrents of destruction assailed me; the snares of death confronted me. In my distress I called upon the Lord, to my God I cried out; from his temple he heard my voice, my cry reached his ears» (Psalm 18:3.7).

In these words of the Psalm the great sufferings, mystical as well, of the foundress Mother are well alluded to, who knew how to unite hope and love, joy and sorrow, «rejoicing like a hero to run his course» (Psalm 19:6).

She knew how to travel the path of holiness and of the apostolate, in the footsteps of Christ suffering and crucified, almost repeating with Jesus: «I have a baptism to be baptized with - the baptism of blood - and how great is my anguish until it is accomplished!» (Lk 12:50). And those words spoken on the eve of the passion: «I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer» (Lk 22:15).

Monday

Tr. pp. 131-132, par. 3.3

The daughters of St. Anne and all who belong to the Family of the Mother of the Immaculate are called to be a prophetic sign of the merciful love of the Father, of the unconditional offering of Christ Jesus, of hope, fruit of the Spirit.

By their very presence they seek to be credible witnesses for all people, so that they may open themselves to salvation and be able to share in the integral freedom brought by Christ. Therefore they comfort, help, make their own the anxieties and concerns of those who suffer; they bring relief to the sick and the marginalized, awakening their hope in the Lord Jesus and in his promises, and help to discover the precious essence of suffering in the light of his passion.

In the suffering and the marginalized they moreover recognize and serve Christ Crucified, who considers done to Himself what is done to the weakest, the most forgotten and the poorest, and they accompany with trust the hopes of man, orienting them towards the path of the covenant which will be definitively fulfilled in the beatific vision, in the splendour of the glory of the Father contemplated eternally.

To achieve this they follow with vigilant readiness the action of the Spirit, and work eagerly to gather around the Father the whole human family in the certainty that only God and his Kingdom are absolute.

Thus, with the whole Church, in prayer and in heart, they cry out day and night: come, Lord Jesus!

Tuesday

TC pp. 210-211, «When the good is not according to the will … off the path»

- When the good is not according to the will of God, it is not perfect. He who created man on his own initiative, to satisfy an ambition and make himself an object of admiration, has no lasting work, his building will soon be torn down.

He listened to me with a certain sarcastic smile; he was little pleased by my words. I said.

«If you do not believe it is the work of the Lord, why do you not try to introduce them on your way?»

«You say it with your lips, but!…

On hearing this, he flies into a rage, shouts and begins to call me names; he threatens to accuse me of having blasphemed because I did not speak according to the doctrine of the Church.

«Do so! my judge is my Master!»

«Then, who are you?»

«See, good shepherd, that you are mistaken, because I am a poor slave who can do nothing else but what my Master has commanded me.

He looks around, and then resumes:

«Tell me, where is this Master of yours? After a long sigh:

«Oh! do you not know him?»

At this answer he calls me a fool; and I see that my time is wasted. He turns and leaves me.

Oh! My Love! this one wants to work and does not know for whom he works nor where?

Folly of the ambitious man! he wants to be, wants to do, and concludes nothing, because he is off the path.

Wednesday

FS pp. 273-275, «Spiritual guide… not to wear herself out»

Spiritual guide and solicitous mother.

We already know the foundress's maternal affection for the spiritual daughters God gave her. Feeling herself responsible before Him who called them and entrusted them to her care communicates to her love a sense of presence among them, united with a lively pastoral awareness that makes her all zeal for their good.

The letters to superiors and to individual sisters attest her delicate maternal attentions, almost meticulous, both as regards bodily health and the interests of the spirit. To express how close she feels to each one she uses terms full of spontaneous cordiality: «I have you with me… everywhere wherever I go»

- «I feel all the sorrows you have and I told the Lord to transfer them onto my shoulders, for my breast already shares in the pain»

- «I have you at my right hand and every morning I commend you to God, my only All»

- «You are nearer to me than if I had you at my side…»

- «I always pray and can say in all truth that no morning passes in which I leave the church without praying in particular for all of you».

She not only shares the afflictions and the vicissitudes of the good religious, who console her heart, but also the situations and struggles of those who are in danger of infidelity to the commitments undertaken; she prays for them, offers her penances for them. She writes on 19 September 1892:

«I had promised the bloody discipline if my Good granted me the conversion of a daughter of St. Anne who was in great danger of losing her vocation… I saw her free and turned wholly to Jesus» (M 12.2, p.

5f).

With her feminine sense of the particular, she keeps in mind all the details of each house. In a letter to Sr. A. Francesca Camisa, superior of the house of Piacenza, she asks her: «How are the flowers? The trees, did they take? Those of the portress will be beautiful: tell her I was very pleased with her labours and that the Holy Mother will keep her alive for many long years, so that she does not wear herself out» (Letter 2-3-1872).

Thursday

D. pp. 83-84, «Walk in my presence … will follow in the ways of God»

«Walk in My Presence…

The Voice again with the usual gentleness: try, it is my wish, and then I said: no, this Voice is my Good because I know it only too well and the ugly one who speaks to me dully is the dragon. And at once I put them on, or rather I made these irons and then put them on. They were on a skin of most atrocious points and I felt nothing, not even that night, they were most gentle pains. Oh! sweet Love what did I gain as a gift? Oh! sweetness (enraptured in Him I enjoyed the most beautiful and dear delights, illustrations) he taught me so many beautiful things» (M. 1.1, p. 138).

Adherence to God, through love, opens the soul to receive a new light. In the new horizon she sees clearly the holiness of God and all that is disharmonious in her and in others.

From this light a new tension is born, which causes a suffering all the greater as it makes the soul perceive the intensity of her natural attachments.

This is how Rosa describes this interior dynamism, the light that enlightens her and the witness of mercy of her Good: «To suffer and to rejoice. Oh! how useful these lights are to me, in a flash I see everything. Oh! what I feel, how I feel myself all aflame and set about correcting that defect with such force because it is an offence to my Good. Be silent, heartless one, why do you offend my dear Crucified? What did he do to you that you (offend him) so barbarously? I feel such pain, but Jesus is silent. Through the depths of his immense mercy, he suffers and does not punish. Oh! My Love, so many times I ask him to take from me this pain I suffer» (M. 1.1, p. 140).

The things that Jesus heard from his Father (cf. Jn 15:15), and makes known to her in mystical union, must not be forgotten.

They are his words and his divine interventions that weave her personal history and that of the Work. These interventions and words, her Good insists several times, she must set down on paper. Because He is the light of her path, she obeys even without being able to foresee that this light will illumine the path of all those who will follow her in the ways of God.

Friday

Tr. pp. 116-117, «Charity sums up … the love of God is perfected in us»

Charity sums up, then, the practice of all the virtues: «it is patient and kind; charity is not jealous, it does not boast, it is not inflated, it is not rude, it does not seek its own interests, it is not quick-tempered, it does not brood over injury, it does not rejoice over wrongdoing but rejoices with the truth. It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things» (1 Cor 13:4-7). Are not the virtues Mother Rosa held so dear: simplicity, humility, meekness, prudence, so many other forms of charity? These virtues are no less companions of hope. It is not possible, in fact, to possess great love for God and neighbour without the sure mirage of hope, faith, hope, charity are inseparable components of Christian perfection. They constitute its substance. This is verified especially when these virtues are lived in the generous gratuitousness and availability proper to a heart «poor and merciful», turned solely to growing in reciprocal communion. Therefore, to live the family spirit in the various states of life, according to the particular vocation of the disciples of Rosa Gattorno, entails: giving oneself generously to one another, as God does (cf. 2 Cor 9:5-14); living mutual understanding, tolerance, respect for the truth present in all (cf. Rom 14); placing the Father at the centre of reciprocal relationship, welcoming his Word and letting oneself be transformed by it; sacrificing oneself according to the example of Christ Jesus, turned to reaching the goal he indicated: «if we love one another… the love of God is perfected in us» (1 Jn 4:12).

Saturday

Tr. pp. 117-118, par. 1.2

The Church is essentially a mystery of communion, «a people brought into unity by the unity of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit» (cf. LG 4).

Fraternal life reflects the depth and richness of such mystery, taking shape as a human space inhabited by the Trinity, which thus extends into history the gifts of communion proper to the three divine persons.

All this requires a path of personal and community growth, learning to overcome conflicts, growing in the capacity for forgiveness, in the exercise of discernment in the light of the Holy Spirit, knowing how to create unity in diversity, fostering and taking part in dialogue, on the unattainable model of the Most Holy Mary.

All the members of Mother Rosa's charismatic Family are called to carry one another's burdens with love, loving the cross as she did, remaining serene in trials and joyful in hope, never forgetting that a charism lived in fullness translates the Gospel, in particular the Gospel of the beatitudes, proclaimed by Jesus in his programmatic discourse, in which he lets it be understood that every virtue and every suffering and contradiction borne out of love of God brings into the soul a beginning of Paradise, in the continual memory of Jesus suffering and of Mary Immaculate-Sorrowful, mother of Grace and Mercy, mother of Hope.

To live, however, a lifestyle that is a witness of fraternity and a proclamation of hope requires a deep life of prayer and of gratuitous self-giving.

33rd Sunday in Ordinary Time

Tr. pp. 49-51, par. 2.4

The divine-human person of Christ Jesus will one day return in glory to judge humanity. Therefore all humanity looks to Him and awaits Him with confidence, for an eternal life, almost a deification of man made, in the most marvellous way, sharer and consort of the infinite, eternal, most blessed life of God, an anticipation and assurance for all those who live in this hope.

It does not seem out of place, therefore, to recall here the waiting and the hope of the old Covenant. In its overall prophetic and foretelling character of the new Covenant, marked by the loftiest desire for the joyful waiting for the encounter with Jesus in glory, the ancient interior cry of prayer: «Come, Lord Jesus!», takes on new vigour, meaning, consistency, impetus. It is an anticipation of Paradise. «Come, Lord Jesus!» not only in human form, but in the splendour of glory. Ultimately Jesus is the first and the last word. The first implicit in the Promise, the last word, explicit, that of the last of the sacred Books: the Apocalypse. Every soul awaits Him, even if it lives in the appearances of the world that flees, even if it seeks Him where He is not, even when it rejects Him because it does not know Him.

With inspired and brilliant intuition Mother Rosa raised the banner of hope as her programme and her charism.

The hope poured out in us by the Spirit, sent by Jesus to all his followers, arouses in us the inextinguishable desire to see God face to face. The Holy Spirit infuses in us, with unutterable groanings, a living and growing expectation of seeing God. What the Psalm says is thus verified: «My soul thirsts for the living God: when shall I come and behold the face of God?» (Ps 42:3).

And what does the soul seek, then, if not to see your Face? This is the unanimous sigh of the old and the new Covenant. Mother Rosa several times mystically contemplated the face of the Father. With this light in her soul she saw well that the face of the Father is made present in the face of the Crucified Son, beloved, guide, dearly loved, eucharist, that divine face which appeared visibly in Jesus, the incarnate Word.

To seek the face of God! In this connatural sigh of the soul, image of God, the spirituality of the old and of the new Covenant are admirably joined.

Monday

D. p. 72, «In this tasting…restored and healed «

In this tasting and contemplating of what Jesus gives her in love, she goes on identifying herself with Him who died so that she might no longer live for herself, but for Him who died and rose (cf. 2 Cor 5:14f). She experiences, like St. Paul, that it is not she who lives, but her Beloved lives in her:

«But, it is not I who live it is my Jesus who lives in me…» (M. 1.1, p. 12).

The call to be configured to Christ Crucified demands of her the price of absolute docility to the will of the Beloved. It entails for her the radicalness of self-giving according to the measure of the gift of the Beloved himself. He, however, supplies her with strength and perseverance in the not easy process of identification with Him:

«…Temptations came upon me and the enemy assailed me with new assaults. The combat is such that I am left without strength, but my Beloved furnished me with his strength to resist» (M. 1.1, pp. 12-15).

«But I am weak, O my Love, give me a little of your strength to be able to resist everything; these words ended, behold I was in perfect calm without pains, as if restored and healed!» (M. 1.1, p. 15).

Tuesday

Tr. pp. 47-48, par. 2.2

The poverty of Jesus is expressed theologically, according to St. Paul, in the fact that the Son of God, from being Lord, creator and king of the universe: «though he was God he emptied himself, took the form and condition of a Servant, assuming human nature in the unity of the divine Person of the Word». He becomes a «servant»! Human nature, then, in comparison with the divine is nothing. Though God, absolute fullness of every good and of every perfection, uniting to himself, personally, human nature, he lowered himself to the poverty of nothingness. He, creator and lord of all, became poor with the poverty of the servant (cf. Phil 2:7).

This supreme humiliation includes in itself also the poverty of Mary, that of the family of St. Anne and St. Joachim, and the humiliation accepted by him in becoming incarnate in the most pure womb of the Immaculate, his Mother.

Jesus accepted the narrow limits of poverty during 30 years of hidden and laborious life in Joseph's workshop, working as a carpenter, he lived the poverty of concealment: «Is he not the carpenter's son?» (Mt 13:55), and also in the three years of public life he openly declared: «Foxes have the security and warmth of their dens, birds their nests, the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head!» (Mt 8:20; Lk 9:58). The poverty of Jesus, therefore, has not only an economic meaning, but takes on a profound theological and spiritual meaning: God who becomes a creature assuming the form of «servant»; to draw near to us God becomes like one of us, with a gesture of infinite love and, finally, lets himself be seized, condemned to death, scourged, crowned with thorns, crucified and even stripped of everything, dying naked on the cross.

How could the charism of Mother Rosa Gattorno, most loving of the Crucified, be explained otherwise, without this theological, ascetic-mystical background which so impressively characterizes her life?

Wednesday

Tr. pp. 104-106, «The daughters (the sons)… of her mission»

The daughters, [the sons] of St. Anne and the other members of the Family follow Christ, the poor one par excellence, and contemplate Mary, who not only stands out among the lowly and the poor of the Lord but transcends them beyond comparison to the point of drawing the gaze of God: «He has looked upon the lowliness of his handmaid». Precisely through this supreme poverty she was filled with the fullness of grace on earth, and of glory in heaven and throughout the centuries of human history: «All generations will call me blessed».

In the Magnificat Mary reveals the praying spirit that synthesizes in herself, in a mature way, the praise, the blessing, the adoration, the supplication, the offering, the waiting, the gratitude of her ancestors, that is, of all those who with their lives glorified God.

She draws reasons for contemplation and exultation from her own personal experience with God, in whom she perceives herself as a link in the long chain of the history of humanity.

Formed in the contemplation of the events and wonders of God handed down by Scripture, shaped early in the sense of personal relationship with Him, as an authentic «poor one», her prayer becomes absolute openness and docility when the mysterious event of the Incarnation involves her in person.

Prayer forms her to grasp all the passages of God in her history and in that of humanity, therefore she proclaims him: my Saviour, Almighty and Holy.

The contemplation of God detaches her from herself to such a point that she sees herself in Him as «handmaid» who, by her humility and fullness, has drawn the divine blessing upon humanity.

As a chosen member of the «Remnant of Israel» Mary nourishes her prayer with the Word of God, and welcomes into her soul the message of the psalms, transforming it into a vital fabric that illumines her action and opens her to the universal embrace of the saving action of her Saviour.

Union with God, the specific vocation of her people, is accomplished in her to such a degree that she becomes, by divine gratuitous grace, the Mother of the eternal Word: the Messiah awaited by Israel, the Redeemer who, associating her with his redemptive plan, makes her Mother of Humanity.

Contemplating Mary, the members of the Family of the holy Mother live their commitment in the church in prayer and poverty of heart, which for them is a way of being, of living and of existing that qualifies their presence in the world and informs their lifestyle, familial and apostolic.

Contemplation, prayer, «poverty of heart which Mother Rosa embodied in her own existence, driven by her ardent desire to identify herself with Christ emptied unto death on a cross, with Him whom she used to call «my Good» and whose very path she longed to travel, her gaze turned to Mary as the accomplished model of what she experienced as her most intimate vocation: «Useless slave of my Jesus, my beloved Paradise»» (Const., art. 6).

The emphasis on the presence of Mary has a great and exceptional significance for the Daughters of St. Anne and for the other followers of Mother Rosa, and makes their spirit understood. In harmony with their very name, it designates them, that is, sisters and brothers of Mary most holy, formed in the same school and continuers of her mission.

Thursday

FS pp. 212-213, «Her mother's heart… most select blessings «

Her mother's heart, when she writes to the daughters of St. Anne, finds no more fitting way of expressing her affection to them than to meet each one in the Heart of Jesus. It would be endless to try to gather the warm expressions in which she affirms at once her love for the Lord and for the addressee.

Every day she made, as it were, an oblation to the eternal Father, in the mercy seat of the Heart of Jesus, of her Institute, not as of an organized and operating structure, but as of a living reality, made up of individual persons, each with her vocation, with her effort of sanctification, with her responsibilities, with her problems. It was her prayer as foundress:

«My God! to you I entrust these creatures whom you have committed to me. Now I place them for all this time in the Heart of your Son Jesus, and may you cover them with heavenly dew, that they may be defended from every least encounter. In this loving retreat of the Heart of Jesus may they learn the true school of your divine Love. My God, bless them and strengthen them in suffering, pour upon them the most select blessings» (Letter to Sr. A. Paola Bucciotti: 25-5-1871).

Friday

Tr. pp. 150-151, «The Church, that is, the kingdom …Christ and the believers «

The church, that is, the kingdom of Christ already present in mystery by the power of God, grows visibly in the world. This beginning and this growth are signified by the blood and water that flowed from the open side of the crucified Christ and are foretold by the words of the Lord about his death on the cross: «And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to myself» (Jn 12:32). Every time the sacrifice of the cross «by which Christ our Paschal Lamb has been sacrificed’ (1 Cor 5:7) is celebrated on the altar, the work of our redemption is renewed. And together with the sacrament of the eucharistic bread, the unity of the faithful who form one body in Christ, who is the light of the world, is represented and brought about; from Him we come, through Him we live, to Him we are directed» (LG 3).

In this truly marvellous sense Jesus is our hope and the church is truly the Ark of the Covenant, prefigured in the old Covenant, divinely realized in the new and eternal Covenant.

The church is therefore the beginning on earth of the kingdom of Christ and of God.

In the light of this splendid theology of the church the various images of the church outlined by the Council are luminously understood: «the church is the sheepfold whose one door is Christ; it is the flock of which Christ himself is the Good Shepherd and prince of shepherds; it is the field of God in which the ancient olive tree grows, whose holy root were the patriarchs…; the church is the building of God of which the Lord is the cornerstone, the foundation on which the church itself is built and from which it will receive stability and cohesion. The church is the house in which his family dwells, the dwelling of God with human beings; it is the new Jerusalem, the Holy City. In it, as living stones, we form a spiritual temple. This holy city St. John, in the Apocalypse, contemplates in its final phase, coming down from God as a bride adorned for her husband» (Rev 21:1ff.).

The church is the heavenly Jerusalem, «our mother», the immaculate bride of the immaculate lamb.

And while the church accomplishes on this earth her pilgrimage far from the Lord (cf. 2 Cor 5:6), she is like an exile who seeks and desires the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God until with her Bridegroom she will appear clothed in glory (cf. Col 3:1-4)» (cf. LG 6,7).

However the image par excellence is the Church as mystical body formed by Christ and by the believers (cf. LG 7).

Saturday

D. p. 182, «Joy of the angels…sound of the angels»

Besides being messengers of God for her mission, the Angels offer Rosa glimpses of deep joy, anticipating moments of endless beatitude. Thus she describes a moment of communion with her Good, who is granting her to see a glimpse of eternity:

«On the day of the Immaculate I added to my vows that of poverty (year 1862)…, the rapture increased…, I felt that something must happen in me… I saw the feast being prepared in heaven. Oh! immense joy: the Saints who had greater splendour, the Angels with garlands went interlacing them; the melody of the sounds, the souls who occupy Paradise, vied with one another to celebrate their advocates. Oh! Paradise how beautiful you are: your joys and your feasts make me die!… the sight of my Good…, so beautiful, those rays, that light, the beauty…!» (M. 1.1, p. 41). Also in one of the visions of Father Bernardo, on the day when he prophesies to her the foundation of the contemplative community in Piacenza and explains to her the prophecy he made when he was visiting the Caracciolo Family, Rosa notes:

«Today I heard the sound of the Angels» (M. 1.1, p. 90).
34th Sunday in Ordinary Time

Solemnity of Christ the King

Tr. p. 49-51, par. 2.4

The divine-human person of Christ Jesus will one day return in glory to judge humanity. Therefore all humanity looks to Him and awaits Him with confidence, for an eternal life, almost a deification of man made, in the most marvellous way, sharer and consort of the infinite, eternal, most blessed life of God, an anticipation and assurance for all those who live in this hope.

It does not seem out of place, therefore, to recall here the waiting and the hope of the old Covenant. In its overall prophetic and foretelling character of the new Covenant, marked by the loftiest desire for the joyful waiting for the encounter with Jesus in glory, the ancient interior cry of prayer: «Come, Lord Jesus!», takes on new vigour, meaning, consistency, impetus. It is an anticipation of Paradise. «Come, Lord Jesus!» not only in human form, but in the splendour of glory. Ultimately Jesus is the first and the last word. The first implicit in the Promise, the last word, explicit, that of the last of the sacred Books: the Apocalypse. Every soul awaits Him, even if it lives in the appearances of the world that flees, even if it seeks Him where He is not, even when it rejects Him because it does not know Him.

With inspired and brilliant intuition Mother Rosa raised the banner of hope as her programme and her charism.

The hope poured out in us by the Spirit, sent by Jesus to all his followers, arouses in us the inextinguishable desire to see God face to face. The Holy Spirit infuses in us, with unutterable groanings, a living and growing expectation of seeing God. What the Psalm says is thus verified: «My soul thirsts for the living God: when shall I come and behold the face of God?» (Ps 42:3).

And what does the soul seek, then, if not to see your Face? This is the unanimous sigh of the old and the new Covenant. Mother Rosa several times mystically contemplated the face of the Father. With this light in her soul she saw well that the face of the Father is made present in the face of the Crucified Son, beloved, guide, dearly loved, eucharist, that divine face which appeared visibly in Jesus, the incarnate Word.

To seek the face of God! In this connatural sigh of the soul, image of God, the spirituality of the old and of the new Covenant are admirably joined.

Monday

Tr. pp. 143-144, «For those he foreknew… we wait for it with perseverance»

For those he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that he might be the firstborn among many brothers; and those he predestined he also glorified» (Rom 8:28-30).

Mother Rosa firmly believed in God's design, and for this she did not spare her life, always hoping, even against all hope, in him, her Good, her fortress and her defender: «Who will bring a charge against God's chosen ones? God is the one who acquits. Who will condemn? Christ Jesus who died, rather, who was raised, who is at the right hand of God, who indeed intercedes for us. What will separate us, then, from the love of Christ? Will anguish, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or the sword?

As it is written: for your sake we are being slain all day long; we are counted as sheep to be slaughtered. No, in all these things we conquer overwhelmingly through him who loved us».

This same certainty must grow in us, so that we may experience in life, in total surrender to the Father, how «neither death, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord» (Rom 8:38-39).

To be children in the Son is our destiny, but it is still the object of our hope. «In hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope; for who hopes for what he sees? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with perseverance» (Rom 8:24-25).

Tuesday

Tr. p. 54, par. 3.1

The hope that the people chosen by God in the Old Testament lived in the covenant pact, stipulated by God with the Patriarchs, with Moses and the Prophets, was founded on the word of God. Hope, the banner of Mother Rosa's spirituality, is founded on the living and unshakeable rock that is Jesus Christ himself.

The people of the new covenant, the church generated by the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, walks in hope, awaiting the final glorious manifestation of Christ.

The presence between heaven and earth of an eternal pontiff who is the incarnate Word cannot fail to have repercussions on human beings. Humanity re-conformed to His head through redemptive suffering, reconsecrated to the Father by the glory of the Son of Man, constitutes the church, which is certainly the people of God, but also the new Eve who is born from the side of the new Adam, asleep on the cross in the sleep of a death that conquers death for ever.

Wednesday

Tr. pp. 54-56, par. 3.2

The church, like Christ himself, is «mystery», that is, manifestation of God who gives himself to the creature. She is the very mystery of the glory of Jesus, considered in the broad, «earthly» sense, but also inclusive of the heavenly church, a marvellous reality like all the works of God.

For these reasons we are not permitted to enter into the knowledge and love of the Son of God dead and risen except through the knowledge and love of the church. It is necessary, however, to distinguish the church mystical body of Christ, enriched by the Holy Spirit, depositary of the treasures of grace and holiness merited by Jesus Christ, whereby she has become his immaculate Bride, called to proclaim Christ to the world and endowed with a prophetic, priestly and royal spirit, from her other aspects which could obscure her reality. To distinguish is therefore «to clarify».

A reality that shares in the mystery and holiness of God demands much accuracy and caution of language. The concept of church briefly outlined casts, nevertheless, no shadow on the holiness of the church itself.

As God in the old Covenant willed the most careful construction of the ark, as a sensible expression of the divine holy and sanctifying presence, so Jesus Christ founded the church as a visible point of reference of his holy and sanctifying presence on earth for the salvation and redemption of human beings, rich in all the gifts and charisms of the Holy Spirit.

The church which in the Creed we proclaim holy because of the people who belong to her, who are not holy, but are called to holiness, it is wisdom to distinguish well from the holy and sanctifying church, icon of the most holy Trinity.

To the church thus understood, that is, holy, do not belong sinners who obstinately remain detached from Jesus Christ through sin. They belong to her, however, only virtually, to the extent, that is, that they repent, and wish to return to Christ and live in the bosom of the church. The church and Christ, in fact, cannot be sharply separated.

Thursday

Tr. pp. 84-87, par. 1.5

Prudence: letting oneself be guided by Love

Simplicity and prudence form an inseparable pair.

The chosen people knew the importance of letting themselves be guided prudently by God, by wisdom (cf. Wis 9:11); in doubt over a choice they were accustomed to respect the supreme dominion of God: «To God belong counsel and prudence» (Job 12:13). From generation to generation the faithful learned: «Learn prudence, you simple ones» (Prov 8:5); «wisdom teaches temperance and prudence» (Bar 9ff.).

In this school St. Anne and Mary her daughter had been educated, enlightened by that prudence which Jesus, as Master, will teach to all humanity.

When he sends his disciples to proclaim the Gospel he indeed warns them: «I am sending you out like sheep among wolves; so be shrewd as serpents and simple as doves» (Mt 10:16).

Jesus' warning continues to hold all its value today, as it did in the time of Mother Rosa, who lived applying to all her choices the criteria of this virtue without separating it from simplicity.

«Prudence is that light which between two things makes you always choose the one that best leads you to gain and to increase the love of God» (Reg. 1869, p. 25).

No virtue stands, therefore, without prudence. The Christian and also pre-Christian moral tradition define prudence, in fact, as the virtue of virtues, the virtue that guides and directs all the others.

A soul consecrated to God, generous, intelligent, industrious, rich in good will, desirous of holiness, humble, pure, poor, docile, if she does not possess prudence exposes all the other virtues to danger. And when the virtues are in danger it is as if one did not have them.

A fine edifice of virtues without the safeguard of prudence is like the house built on sand of which Jesus speaks in the Gospel (cf. Mt 7:26).

Prudence is therefore the firm rock on which the edifice of the other virtues stands. It regulates, indeed perfects, all the moral virtues. This most important virtue guides the person in the sphere of action, in the choice of the things to be done to attain Christian perfection and holiness. The very recent Constitutions take up, in a modern style, with great fidelity and finesse, the teaching of the Rule of 1869:

«Simplicity, which «cannot live without the company of prudence», constitutes with it an inseparable pair which, sincerely lived, leads to the possession of true wisdom… Christ is not only the Master who teaches the practice of this virtue, but his very person constitutes the foundation of Christian prudence because He is the sole and absolute criterion that enables one to discern and judge the various spirits…» (Const., art. 19).

How fitting and wise it is to make prudence equivalent to wisdom! The virtue of prudence practised according to the criteria of the Rule of 1869 and more fully in the very recent edition, approved by the Holy See, constitutes a most valuable help for walking safely on the path of perfection.

Friday

Tr. pp. 149-150, «The Church according to Vat. Council II… kingdom of Christ and of God»

The church, according to the Second Vatican Council, is «the image of the invisible God».

Marvellously prepared in the history of the people of Israel and in the old Covenant and instituted in the last times, she was manifested by the outpouring of the Spirit and will have glorious fulfilment at the end of the ages. Then, as we read in the holy Fathers, all the just, beginning from Adam, «from the just Abel to the last of the elect», will be gathered together with the Father in the universal church (cf. LG 2).

Earthly and visible church and heavenly invisible church are distinct but not separable. It is the same one church.

«Christ, to fulfil the will of the Father, inaugurated the kingdom of heaven on earth and revealed to us the mystery of Him and by obedience accomplished redemption. The church, that is, the kingdom of Christ already present in mystery by the power of God, grows visibly in the world. This beginning and this growth are signified by the blood and water that flowed from the open side of the crucified Christ and are foretold by the words of the Lord about his death on the cross: «And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to myself» (Jn 12:32). Every time the sacrifice of the cross «by which Christ our Paschal Lamb has been sacrificed’ (1 Cor 5:7) is celebrated on the altar, the work of our redemption is renewed. And together with the sacrament of the eucharistic bread, the unity of the faithful who form one body in Christ, who is the light of the world, is represented and brought about; from Him we come, through Him we live, to Him we are directed» (LG 3).

In this truly marvellous sense Jesus is our hope and the church is truly the Ark of the Covenant, prefigured in the old Covenant, divinely realized in the new and eternal Covenant.

The church is therefore the beginning on earth of the kingdom of Christ and of God.

Saturday

Tr. pp. 74-75, «The daughters of St. Anne …summit of holiness»

The daughters of St. Anne, and all the other members of the Family of the holy mother of Mary Immaculate, are charismatically called to live Jesus our Hope, a characteristic which distinguishes their spirit, linking itself in a particular way to the holiness of the mother of the Immaculate. This peculiar aspect of the spirituality of Mother Rosa's charismatic Family unmistakably marks the charism inherited from the Foundress, stamped by the spirituality of waiting lived by the mother of the Immaculate, and conforms it to the authentic classical spirituality of the catholic church: «To live the Covenant in Christ Jesus, our hope».

Among the theological virtues the virtue of hope therefore stands out. This emphasis takes nothing from the substance of Christian spirituality of all times and characterizes the charism well. One may say that the charismatic primacy of Hope is enriched by one more point compared with the spirituality of the other religious Families, almost as if the followers of Mother Rosa wished to superimpose on the waiting for glorious Jesus the meaningful long waiting of the chosen people, lived in all its fullness by St. Anne and by her most holy Daughter.

The emphasis on the theological virtue of hope implies vigilance, the virtue most strongly inculcated by: «Stay awake and pray, because at the hour you least expect, the Son of Man will come»; «Watch and pray» (Mt 25:13). This is the attitude of persons who abhor the great enemy of spiritual progress which is lukewarmness, sloth, and the spiritual sleep that blocks the step of ascent towards the heights of the interior life.

Precisely this vigilant and watchful constancy in prayer led Mother Rosa to the summits of holiness.

Other Feasts

8 December, Immaculate Conception

D. pp. 143-144, «The Immaculate One whom she loves…the motherhood of Anne»

The Immaculate One whom she loves, the One chosen by God, preserved from sin, the Most Holy Virgin, the Mother of Jesus, therefore indicates to her that the Father, in his plan of love, wishes to exalt Anne also, her Mother. He wishes to say a word to the Church and to the world about Anne. He wishes the poor and the suffering to know and venerate her who collaborated with Him so that the creature chosen to be Mother of Jesus might remain whole, humble, faithful to the Covenant and open to the promises of the Messiah, Servant and Saviour of the world.

Rosa welcomes the will of the Father who sends her into the world as a sign and prolongation of the motherhood of Anne, a reflection of his fatherhood. From this fatherhood, in fact, source and origin of all fatherhood and motherhood on earth, derives the maternal identity and the mission of Mary, the maternal event of Anne. An event that introduces into the world her who by pure grace was conceived without sin as the humblest creature and the one most capable of receiving the ineffable gift of the Almighty.

This mystery of the fatherhood of God, made manifest in the motherhood of Anne and above all in that of Mary, is welcomed by Rosa who celebrates it with her life and works in the Church and in the world.

The motherhood of Anne, in fact, is also a reflection of the divine motherhood of Mary: since she was predestined from eternity as Mother of the Divine Redeemer (LG 61), as such she qualifies and makes the motherhood of Anne an expression of the one and eternal motherhood.

2 February, Presentation of the Lord

D. pp. 140-142, par. 5

In the Mother and the Child all the promises of the Father are fulfilled with infinite mercy and humility. The motherhood of Mary is the privileged vehicle for the realization of God's entry into history and of his triumph over the evil one.

In the womb of the woman, who was to crush the head of the serpent, the Son of God truly took flesh, not disdaining human frailty. The way of triumph over evil passes through this total dedication to humanity. Mary-Mother is the tangible sign of the infinite mercy of God and the infinite humility of the God-Man, who has pitched his tent among us. Rosa receives as a gift the certainty that in weakness the strength of the presence and intercession of the Mother of Christ triumphs:

«…new tribulations came upon me that tore me apart, so strong were they…, but dear Mother Mary was not slow to come and comfort me, appearing to me together with the dear Child, my Beloved. Oh what comfort! But the evil serpent… always brought new torments…» (M. 1.1, p. 55).

The work that God accomplished in Mary by associating her with the saving mystery of the Son has permanent value. The effectiveness of the Mother's mission, for every time and person who lets himself be guided docilely by her, is for Rosa an experience that generates full adherence to the Economy of God who sends the Son to bring it to fulfilment: «Behold, a Son comes into the world, the «offspring of the woman», who will defeat the evil of sin at its roots:

«he will crush the head of the serpent»… Mary, Mother of the Word, is placed at the centre of that enmity, of that struggle which accompanies the history of humanity on earth and the history of salvation itself» (RM 1).

25 March, Annunciation of the Lord

Tr. pp. 51-52, par. 2.5

Closely and indissolubly associated with the work of redemption «as generous companion and altogether exceptional cooperator of her Son the Redeemer» (cf. LG 61), Mary most holy, the humble handmaid of the Lord offered totally to the person and work of Christ, is under Him and with Him at the service of the mystery of redemption, becoming a cause of salvation.

What a marvellous opening to hope the mother of God and our mother is, therefore, for us!

God wished to reach us through the powerful mediation and the maternal help of Mary.

Mother Rosa is clear about this precise identity and the most lofty mission of Mary in God's saving plan. For this reason, in calling the members of her spiritual Family «Daughters» [and Sons] of St. Anne she does nothing other than place at the centre the maternal function of Mary most holy, inasmuch as the presence of St. Anne clearly points to the prodigious power and greatness of her Daughter, Immaculate and most holy, proclaimed our mother by Jesus on Calvary, constituted forever mediatrix to the Mediator (cf. God's Gift…, pp. 137-138; 142-143), Mother par excellence of all humanity.

In this sense one can then well understand why God wished that all graces should come to us through the hands of Mary.

Last Saturday of May

Mary Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae

D. pp. 145-147, par. 8

The privilege of Mary, Mother of Grace and Mercy, expresses her dignity and function in the Economy of Salvation: «By conceiving Christ, bearing him… suffering with her dying Son, …she cooperated in an altogether special way in the work of the Saviour… to restore supernatural life to souls. For this reason she was a Mother to us in the order of grace»; - «And this motherhood of Mary in the Economy of grace endures without pause… until the perpetual crowning of all the elect» (LG 61;62).

Rosa enjoys the gift of the presence of Mary Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae who reveals her role in relation to the Church and to all humanity: She cooperated in a special way in the work of the Saviour with obedience, faith, hope and ardent charity so that every person might become a child in the Son.

Rosa preciously guards the presence of the Mother of Grace and Mercy not only in her heart, but also in the image.

Mary Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae accompanies her in the development of the work and in her personal journey:

«My angel Bernardo appeared to me with his little Madonna…»;

«Oh Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae! Behold she appeared to me and assured me of healing…»;

«She gave me strength…»;

«…behold the little Madonna…! The Child held in his hand a chalice which he wanted to offer me…, and She was holding it. It was a moving sight…, dear Mary conquers» (M. 1.1, p. 83; 5.1, p. 146-147; 5.1, p. 100).

Mary does not abandon Rosa until the last moment of her life. Her last greeting is for Mary Mater Gratiae et Misericordiae. The grace and mercy of God mediated by Mary envelops her throughout her life. For her it is experience what for others is an object of faith: «Not only is the dignity of this motherhood unique and unrepeatable in the history of the human race, but unique also is Mary's participation in the divine plan of man's salvation through the mystery of the Redemption… The eternal love of the Father draws near to each of us through this Mother…» (RH 22).

6 August, Transfiguration of the Lord

D. pp. 116-117, par. 3

The manifestations of God through the Cloud, in Exodus, are referred to throughout the whole history of Salvation. Moreover, other experiences confirm the theological value of the Cloud, the mysterious place of God's presence: «The glory of the Lord in the form of a Cloud filled the Temple built by Solomon»

(1 Kgs 8:10f). In Isaiah: «…the doorposts shook at the voice of him who cried out, while the temple filled with smoke» (Is 6:4).

On the day of Jesus' transfiguration, the apostles, after contemplating «Moses and Elijah who spoke with Jesus of his departure which he was going to accomplish in Jerusalem» (Lk 9:30), enter the cloud and «from the luminous cloud came a voice that said: this is my beloved Son, listen to him» (Mt 17:5; Mk 9:6; Lk 9:34).

The presence of Moses and Elijah represents the Old Testament which attests the passion of the Servant. The figure of the Servant reappears in the voice and in the theophany associated with the cloud (cf. Ex 24:15-16; 40:34-38). Luke wants to say that in Jesus and in his action God is present, intervenes, that God approves the acceptance Jesus has made of his suffering messianism. And since the Cloud indicates the presence of the Spirit, the whole Trinity was present at the Transfiguration. The Father in the voice, the Son in the man, the Spirit in the luminous cloud.

Guided by the light that radiates from this message, and in particular from the other verse of the same pericope: «And while he was praying, his face changed in appearance and his clothing became dazzling white», we read the passage that follows:

«That cloud which I frequently saw, now I see more rarely. The other evening it appeared to me far more luminous than usual, while it stood before me and dazzled me, behold it expands and I see in it my Beloved: He was in it, of infinite beauty, a splendour I know not to what to compare. What he says to me, what he brings me! Everything sweetened my pains, everything made me forget. The tribulations, though not few, she remembers nothing of them. My love alone had absorbed everything, he left me something I cannot explain, but I feel in me that it makes me die of love! From all sides the tribulations, the pains rained down, but how to feel them! Nothing! In my love everything remains absorbed in the sweetness of his love» (M. 1.1, p. 157).

15 August, Assumption of Mary

D. p. 147, par. 9

The Father wished to show Rosa also the presence of Mary, Queen of heaven.

Mary, Mother, Immaculate, virgin, Queen of the Universe, associated with the glory of her Son, is contemplated also in this aspect of the fullness of her glory:

«I saw so beautiful a feast in Heaven, the Sovereign Mary is seated at the Right…»;

«…I saw the Sovereign of heaven and earth surrounded by Angels and Seraphim! Oh beloved Mother…» (M. 1.1, p. 153);

«I had the consolation of seeing the commemoration in heaven of the Sovereign Virgin»;

«A fire was devouring me…» (M. 1.1, pp. 38, 153; 12.1, p. 145).

The vision of the fullness of the mystery of Mary associated with the Mystery of the Son is for Rosa an irradiation of the Trinitarian Life, present in grace and mercy, in the divine motherhood which, in Christ, with Christ and through Christ, is present in the generation of all the children of God.

8 September, Nativity of Mary

Tr. p. 42, «God answered in a…are silent on this point

God answered in a prodigious way the prayer of his most faithful servant, choosing her for a unique mission in the history of salvation, the mission of mother of the Immaculate, of mother of the Mother of God. In her, therefore, the waiting of the old Covenant is fulfilled and the radiant dawn of the new Covenant begins to shine.

In the order of divine Providence God confers special graces on those whom he calls to a particular mission in the work of Redemption.

If St. Anne was called by God to be mother of the Immaculate - Mother of his divine Son - we can surely believe, relying on grounds of great fittingness, that she had uncommon illuminations and mystical communications, even though the Gospels are silent on this point.
